Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 1:

(p-200) Surat al-Nur

Its purpose is the meaning of its name, which is deposited in its heart, namely that He, exalted is He, has all-encompassing knowledge, from which follows complete power, from which follows the establishment of matters upon the utmost wisdom, from which follows the affirmation of the nobility of the Prophet (ﷺ), from which follows the nobility of those whom He chose for his companionship according to their degrees of nearness to him and their special closeness to him, and from which follows the utmost purity, nobility and cleanness of Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), with whom the Prophet (ﷺ) died while he was pleased with her, and she herself died (may Allah be pleased with her) righteous and virtuous. This is the primary purpose, but establishing it requires those premises. (In the name of Allah) Whose word is complete, so His power is dazzling. (The Most Merciful) by whose all-embracing mercy all realities became manifest. (The Most Compassionate) who ennobled whoever He chose for His service.

When the preceding surah had established the prohibition of fornication and the exhortation to chastity, and ended that verse with mention of Paradise, which implies resurrection, He proved this and mentioned what follows from it of warning and action until the surah concluded. At its end He informed of the rebuke of the obstinate (p-201) on the Day of Regret with His saying: ﴿Were not My signs recited to you, and you used to deny them?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 105] and His saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115]. All of that is mercy from Him to His creation, so that whoever He decreed for happiness might return from among them. Then He concluded with His saying: ﴿And You are the best of the merciful﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 118]. So He, glory be to Him, began this surah by bestowing favour upon those addressed by explaining the rulings for which they were created, because they were not created in vain, but for obligations by which He made them worship Him, which remove discord and cut off the root of evil, thereby necessitating mercy and compassion through soundness of heart, given the kinship that exists among them. So He said, informing about a subject whose implied reference is: this is ﴿a surah﴾, that is, a great one. Then He encouraged compliance with what is in it, clarifying that its indefiniteness (tanwin) is for magnification, with His saying: ﴿We sent it down﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness and perfect knowledge and power; ﴿and We made it obligatory﴾, that is, We established it, decreed it, multiplied in it the obligations and affirmed them; ﴿and We sent down in it﴾ with the all-encompassing scope of Our knowledge ﴿signs﴾ of prescribed penalties, rulings, admonitions, parables and others, establishing them as proof, ﴿clear﴾, with no ambiguity in them, as a mercy from Us to you. Whoever entered into the call of our Prophet (ﷺ), which We taught him at the end of that surah, was shown mercy by the Best of the Merciful. Whoever refused it went astray and fell under the rebuke with Our saying: ﴿Were not My signs recited to you﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 105] and the like. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿so that you may remember﴾, that is, so that you may be — if you reflect upon it together with the preceding verses of softening admonitions and warning narratives (p-202) — in hope, according to one who does not know the outcomes, that you might remember, even a kind of remembrance, as the idgham (assimilation) indicates, through the wisdoms you see in it, that the One who set it up for you and detailed it to what you see does not leave you without purpose, so that you turn to all His commands and refrain from His prohibitions, that He may forgive you for what you fell short of in His obedience and show you mercy by bestowing what you cannot reach except through His mercy, and that you may also remember through what makes clear to you matters and unveils the rulings which the veils of the souls had concealed and which the darkness of desires had covered — that which human beings are created with — so that you know that what you love to be done to you by others' love, you should do to them, and what you dislike of that, others dislike too; this will move you toward fairness, which yields purity, affection and loyalty, so that you become among the believers, the successful, the inheritors, who have entered into the call of the bringer of good tidings and warner, with mercy.

Imam Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said in his Burhan: When Exalted is He said ﴿And those who guard their private parts﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 5], then said ﴿So whoever seeks beyond that, those are the transgressors﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 7], the discourse required an explanation of the ruling on the transgressor in this matter, which was not clarified there, so He clarified it in Surat al-Nur, saying ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterer﴾ [al-Nur: 2] — the verse. Then He followed this with the ruling on li'an (mutual imprecation) and qadhf (false accusation), and along with that came the report (p-203) of the story of the slander, as a warning to believers against the slips of tongues, speaking about the unseen without knowledge ﴿and you consider it trivial, but it is tremendous in the sight of Allah﴾ [al-Nur: 15]. Then He followed this, after the threat against those who love the spread of indecency among the believers, with His saying ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unaware, believing women﴾ [al-Nur: 23] — the verses; then with warning against entering houses except after the lawful seeking of permission; then with the command to lower the gaze for men and women, and the prohibition on women from displaying adornment except to those whom Allah, glory be to Him, named in the verse. These purposes recur in this surah up to mention of the ruling on the three times of nakedness (awrat), and entering the houses of relatives and kin. All of this is of what clears a believer's obligation by adhering to what Allah commanded in it and standing at the limits He set, lest he be among the transgressors blamed in His saying ﴿So whoever seeks beyond that, those are the transgressors﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 7]. As for what intervened between the mentioned verses and was linked to them from what is not of the mentioned ruling, it is because the verses drew it in and called for it, and as a place where that is completed and its connection to the interpretation is explained. It is not part of our condition here — and Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, grants us success in understanding His Book — end.

(p-204) Since the foundation of this abode [the world] rests on lineages in inheritance, leadership, marriage, and other matters, and the foundation of that abode [the Hereafter] rests on deeds, due to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So there will be no kinship among them that Day﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101], and since He had urged, at the end of that [discussion], toward concealment and mercy, He warned, out of His mercy at the beginning of this [surah], against the mixing of lineages, the earning of dishonor, and the severing of ties. He made clear that concealment and tenderness are not universal, but are limited by what He, glory be to Him, has defined. So He said, addressing the leaders and those whom they appoint: ﴿The adulteress﴾, that is, the woman who has committed zina, which is the insertion of a private part into a private part that is desired by nature and forbidden by the Law. He mentioned her first because the effect of zina appears upon her in pregnancy and the loss of virginity, and because she is the source of temptation by violating the veil of concealment, guarding, and caution that she was commanded to observe. ﴿And the adulterer﴾.

Since "al" (the definite article) carries the meaning of the relative pronoun, He introduced the fa' (the particle "then") into the predicate and said: ﴿flog﴾, that is, strike. Although its original sense is striking with a whip, which is the lash, ﴿each one of them﴾ [is to be flogged] if he is not muhsan (married and free), but is mukallaf (legally responsible) and bikr (unmarried), as the noble Sunnah has explained, ﴿with a hundred lashes﴾. He began with the hadd (the prescribed punishment) for zina, referred to at the beginning of that [discussion] with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are the transgressors﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 7]. In the use of the word jald (lash), which is the striking with a lash, there is an indication that it is to be severe, to the extent that it exceeds the pain to reach the flesh.

Since this was evident in the abandonment of compassion for them, He stated it explicitly (p-205), because it is the nature of everyone who is liable to fall into such a thing that he would show mercy to them. So He said: ﴿And let not pity for them overtake you﴾, that is, in any state whatsoever, ﴿pity﴾, that is, softness. Perhaps He expressed it with this word to inform [us] that He did not forbid mercy in general, because ra'fah is the most intense or the most tender form of mercy, and it arises from causes in the one who is pitied. Likewise His saying: ﴿in the religion of Allah﴾, that is, which the King, encompassing all attributes of perfection, has legislated for you. This is an indication that what is prohibited is a mercy that leads to abandoning the hadd, or any part of it, or to laxity regarding it, or to approval of the one who violates it, not the tenderness of heart with which humans are naturally created. This is like what is related of Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, that he wept on the day Cyprus (Qubrus) was conquered and the necks of some of its captives were struck. It was said to him: "This is a day of joy!" He said: "It is so, but I weep out of mercy for these servants who disobeyed Allah, so He abandoned them and gave them over to [their enemies]."

When He, glory be to Him, knew what He had created His servants with of mercy toward one another, and He urged this ruling by command and prohibition, He increased the stirring toward it and the exhortation to it with His saying: ﴿if you are [truly] believers in Allah﴾, that is, with that which is like an innate disposition that never separates from [a believer], ﴿in Allah﴾, that is, the Greatest King, who is the Most Merciful of the merciful. He did not legislate that except as a mercy for people in general and for the two fornicators in particular. Whoever reduces a single lash has claimed that he is more merciful than Him, and whoever adds a single lash has supposed that he is wiser and greater than Him.

(p-206) Since He reminded [them] of faith, a condition of which is commitment to the rulings, and since hope tends to dominate a human being, He followed it with what instills fear, and said: ﴿and the Last Day﴾, on which He will call to account for the tiniest speck, the thinnest membrane, the hidden, and the manifest. Since disgrace and exposure are greater to some people than the striking of the sword, let alone the striking of the whip, He said: ﴿And let a group﴾, that is, let them be present in full presence, ﴿witness their punishment﴾, that is, a company that can encircle them, meaning surround them and gather around each of the two, ﴿of the believers﴾ [of both kinds]. [This is] to publicize their affair as a deterrent to them. It is related from Nasr ibn 'Alqamah that this [witnessing] is so that prayers may be made for them for repentance and mercy. In all of this there is a clear indication that the establishment of the hudud and severity in them is among His mercies, glory be to Him, referred to by His saying: ﴿And You are the best of the merciful﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 118].

When it was the case that such severity against the fornicator, for what he has committed of the forbidden that is marked by disgrace, included what conveys the need to avoid him, [Allah] made it explicit, prohibiting marriage to one marked by fornication, male or female. This informs that intercourse with anyone marked by it, whether man or woman, is nothing but fornication, even if it is done under a contract. He said, connecting it to what precedes: (p-207) ﴿The fornicator does not marry﴾, meaning does not wed, ﴿except a fornicatress or a polytheist﴾. That is, one known to be marked by fornication is restricted in marriage to a fornicatress or a polytheist, and that is forbidden. This is a deterrent to the believing woman from marrying one marked by fornication, since he is equated with a polytheist if she lives with him. This comes back to the point that whoever marries a fornicator is either a fornicatress or a polytheist, meaning she is like him or worse than him. Had he limited himself to this, there would be no prohibition against a chaste man marrying a fornicatress. So He, exalted, said prohibiting that: ﴿And the fornicatress—none marries her﴾, meaning does not wed her, ﴿except a fornicator or a polytheist﴾. That is, one known to be marked by fornication is restricted in marriage to a fornicator or a polytheist, and that is forbidden. This is a deterrent to the believing man from marrying one marked by fornication, since she is equated with a polytheist in this. It comes back to the point that whoever marries a fornicatress is either a fornicator or a polytheist, meaning he is like her or worse than her. He attributed the marriage in both places to the man, as an alert that women have no right to conduct the contract itself. Then he stated explicitly what the beginning of the verse had implied, saying in the passive voice, because that suffices the believer to whom the address is directed: ﴿And that has been forbidden﴾, meaning the marriage of the fornicator and the fornicatress, as a prohibition admitting no exception, ﴿upon the believers﴾. From this it is known that the mention of the polytheist male and female is for the sake of greater deterrence. Then this ruling was abrogated, as our imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, agreeing with Ibn al-Musayyab, by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And marry the unmarried among you﴾ [al-Nur: 32]. The word is the plural of ayyim, who is one without a spouse, male or female. So it became permissible for the fornicator (p-208) to marry whomever he wishes, and for the fornicatress to marry whomever she wishes. The reading of the one who read (لا يَنْكِحْ, "let him not marry") in the jussive form comes back to this, because a command may come in the form of a report just as a report may come in the form of a command. And Allah knows best. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him and be pleased with him, said in al-Umm, in a section on the rulings of the Qur'an and in a section after the Book of the Major and Minor Hajj and the Sacrifices: "What has come concerning the marriage of those who have been punished (al-muhdathin)." He mentioned the verse and said: The people of tafsir (exegesis) have differed greatly regarding this verse. Muslim ibn Khalid informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, that this verse was revealed concerning prostitutes of the Jahiliyya who had banners at their dwellings. He said in the other section: "And they were not chaste women, so some of the Muslims wished to marry them, and the verse was revealed prohibiting that they marry anyone except one who makes public the same as they made public, or a polytheist." It was also said: they were polytheist fornicatresses, so it was revealed that none marries them except a fornicator like them or a polytheist, even if he is not a fornicator. And that was forbidden to the believers. It was also said: it is general, but it was abrogated. Sufyan informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: it is abrogated, abrogated by the saying

﴿And marry the unmarried among you﴾ [al-Nur: 32], so they are among the unmarried of the Muslims. This is, as Ibn al-Musayyab said, if Allah the Exalted wills, and upon it (p-209) are proofs from the Book and the Sunna. Then he argued for the corruption of any view other than this, by saying that if the fornicatress is a polytheist, she is forbidden to the fornicating and non-fornicating men of the Muslims, by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And do not marry polytheist women until they believe﴾ [al-Baqara: 221], and there is no disagreement on this. If she is a Muslim, then by Islam she is forbidden to all polytheists in every kind of marriage, by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So if you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾ [al-Mumtahana: 10], and there is no disagreement on this either. And also, there is no disagreement among any of the people of knowledge that idolatresses are forbidden, whether they are chaste or fornicatresses, to whoever believes, whether he is a fornicator or chaste. And also, the Prophet ﷺ lashed a virgin for fornication and lashed a woman, and we do not know that he said to the fornicator: "Do you have a wife, so that she becomes unlawful to you if you commit fornication?" And this fornicator does not marry, nor does the fornicatress marry, except a fornicatress or a fornicator. Indeed, it is even narrated that a man complained to him about his wife's immorality, and he said: "Divorce her." He said: "I love her." He said: "Enjoy her." This refers to what Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and others narrated: "From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'My wife does not refuse the hand of one who touches her.' He said: 'Divorce her.' He said: 'I cannot bear to be without her.' He said: 'Then keep her.'"

Al-Bayhaqi and al-Tabarani narrated it from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, and our shaykh Ibn Hajar said: it is a hadith hasan sahih (good and sound). End. Al-Shafi'i said: It has been narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him (p-210), that he said to a man who wished to marry a woman who had become a fornicatress: "Marry her in the marriage of a chaste Muslim woman." End, in meaning. He said in the section after the Hajj: "So we have found the indication from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a fornicating woman and a fornicating man among the Muslims, that we do not know him to have forbidden either of them to marry other than a fornicatress or a fornicator, nor did he forbid either of them to his spouse." Then he said: "So the preference for a man is not to marry a fornicatress, and for a woman not to marry a fornicator. If the two do it, it is not forbidden to either of them; the disobedience of either of them in itself does not make lawful what is permitted unlawful when one comes to it." Then he said: "And whether the fornicator among them has been punished with the hadd or not punished, or evidence was established against him, or he confessed, the fornication of either of them does not make unlawful the lawful, nor does their fornication, nor any disobedience among the disobediences, except that their religions differ in polytheism and faith." End.

It is known that it was not meant that this ruling was abrogated by the verse of the unmarried alone, but by what was joined to it of consensus (ijma') and other verses and hadiths, in such a way that this made its indication upon what it covers certain, like the indication of the specific upon what it covers. So it is not said that al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, opposed his principle that the specific is not abrogated by the general, because what the specific covers is certain, and what the general covers is apparent and presumptive. This ruling, which is the prohibition at the beginning of Islam after the Hijra, was so that the state of the corrupter would not overcome the reformer, and thus part of the matter would be disrupted, as was indicated in al-Baqara

﴿And do not marry polytheist women﴾ [al-Baqara: 221], and in (p-211) al-Ma'ida at ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become void﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 5]. And this is from the valley of the saying:

"Do not ask about the man, but ask about his companion, for every intimate friend follows the way of his intimate."

Kinship is the cause of union, similarity is the cause of connection, and difference necessitates distance and forbids affinity. Abu Dawud in al-Adab and al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, and he said: hasan gharib, narrated from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "A man is upon the religion of his close friend, so let each of you look at whom he takes as a close friend." Imam Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili narrated in his Musnad, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in narrated to us, Sa'id ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from 'Amra bint 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: There was a woman in Makkah who was a joker, that is, she then emigrated to the noble city of Madina, and she stayed with a woman resembling her, and that reached 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and she said: "My love spoke truly! I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Souls are armies mobilized; those among them that recognize each other are joined, and those among them that deny each other are divided.'" He said: I do not know except that he said in the hadith: "And we do not know that woman." It will come at ﴿And good things are for good men﴾ [al-Nur: 26] the takhrij of "Souls are armies mobilized." Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Marwan al-Dinawari said in the Kitab al-Mujalasa: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Khazzaz narrated to us (p-212), Mus'ab ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ghuzayya al-Ansari, who said: al-Sha'bi said: "It is said that Allah has an angel appointed to gather similar forms, some to others." End. Our shaykh, the hafiz Abu al-Fadl ibn Hajar, attributed it in his takhrij of the hadiths of the Musnad al-Firdaws to Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "with the composition of forms." It is narrated that the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, addressed the people of Kufa three days after his arrival among them, and said: "O people of Kufa, we know your wicked from your good." They said: "How, when you have only three days?" He said: "There were with us wicked and good, so our good joined your good, and our wicked joined your wicked."

When the rulings were settled, and the specific and the general submitted, and the religion stood firm on its foundations, and there was no fear of a breach in any part of its structure, the prohibition was abrogated, and the reprehensibility remained, or the opposite of the preferable. And Allah is the Granter of success. All of this is a preparation for the innocence of 'A'isha, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, as its clarification will come in ﴿And good things are for good men﴾ [al-Nur: 26], because she is the consort of the best of the worlds, the most pious and the most chaste of them; and because each of her and Safwan, may Allah be pleased with both of them, is far from what was charged against them, well known for its opposite. To this points the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Who will excuse me regarding a man whose harm has reached my family? By Allah, I know nothing about my family except good, and they have mentioned a man about whom I know nothing but good." (p-213) And in another narration: "I never knew anything bad about him, and he never entered my house except that I was present." And by the saying of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, about Safwan, may Allah be pleased with him: "He was killed as a martyr in the way of Allah." This is apart from the explicit verses and the evident signs. So ﴿And the good men﴾ [al-Nur: 26] is an allusion before explanation, and an explicit statement and indication after expression and clarification, so that in the innocence of the Truthful one, may Allah be pleased with her, there come together two rational, witnessed proofs that surround the transmitted proof, and become a barrier around it and a protection from any aiming of a charge at it. In that is such a magnitude of her matter and great rank that no one can estimate it at its true worth except the One who specified her with it.

When Allah, glory be to Him, forbade marrying those characterized by fornication, whether a man or a woman, and began with the woman, because a woman's marriage to a fornicator is a likely sign of her own fornication, He turned to warning women against being associated with what suggests that merely marrying someone known to be an adulterer permits calling them adulteresses. This came after He had begun the discussion of the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) for fornication with the female, because her fornication is greater in evil and more shameful and harmful. He then joined to that the prohibition of slander (qadhf), by what requires great eagerness for concealment, guarding honour, and hiding indecency. So He said, mentioning the plural because the ruling of imposing the ḥadd on the accuser (p-214) implies imposing it on one person a fortiori, and there is no ambiguity in this, since when a plural is matched with a plural it conveys distribution: ﴿And those who accuse﴾, that is, of fornication, ﴿chaste women﴾, the plural of muḥṣana (chaste woman). Here it means a free, adult, Muslim, chaste woman. What is meant is slander with fornication, as the context before and after indicates, whether the accusers are men or women, as the relative pronoun conveys. He specified women, although the ruling is general for men, to draw attention to the great right of the Mother of the Believers, ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and because speech about them is more heinous.

Since the one who boldly commits slander, along with the conditions that must be met to avert the ḥadd, shows a desire for concealment that is far-fetched, He indicated this with the particle of delay (ḥarf al-tarākhī, the particle indicating a later sequence), saying: ﴿Then they do not bring﴾, that is, to the judge, ﴿four witnesses﴾, male, ﴿then flog them﴾, O believers, [i.e., the] rulers and their deputies, ﴿eighty lashes﴾ for each one of them, for each chaste woman, if the accuser is not a slave, if they are free. The punishment for a slave is half of that, according to the verse of the chapter of women: ﴿Upon them is half of the punishment for chaste women﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 25]. So this verse is specified by that one, since there is no difference between male and female, nor between the ḥadd for fornication and the ḥadd for slander. ﴿And do not accept from them﴾, that is, after their slander in this manner, ﴿any testimony﴾ (p-215) whatsoever, ﴿ever﴾, because they have been judged to be liars. Whoever is proven to have lied loses reliance on his word.

Since the implied meaning is: "Indeed they have slandered," He joined to it a warning against rashness without verification: ﴿And those, that is, those whose censure was previously mentioned for slander, so that their rank has fallen greatly, ﴿they are the defiantly disobedient (al-fāsiqūn)﴾, that is, they are judged to be defiantly disobedient, and this attribute of defiance is established for them even if the accuser among them is in fact truthful.

Since it was a principle of al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) that an exception (istithna') that follows a sequence of connected clauses joined by "and" (wa) refers back to all of them, whether they are of one kind or several, unless some indicator prevents it, he (al-Biqa'i) here restricted the exception to the sin of slander (fisq) and the rejection of their testimony, but not to the flogging, because completing repentance requires submitting to the prescribed punishment (hadd) and seeking the victim's pardon for it. Another indicator is that this is a right of a human being (haqq adami), which is not cancelled by repentance. This is found in His saying, ﴿except those who repent﴾, meaning they turned back from what they had fallen into of slander and other things, regretted it, and resolved not to return to it, as he explained in al-Baqarah in His saying, ﴿except those who repent, amend, and make clear﴾ [al-Baqarah: 160]. He also indicated that the flogging is not cancelled by repentance through His saying, pointing with the inserted preposition to the fact that the acceptance of repentance does not depend on its extending over the time that follows: ﴿after that﴾, meaning after the matter that required their banishment from testimony, namely the accusation (ramy) and the flogging (jald). Repentance does not change the ruling on the accuser concerning the flogging, but it changes it regarding the rejection of testimony and what results from it, namely the sin (fisq). He indicated the conditions of repentance through His saying, ﴿and amend﴾, meaning after repentance, by the passing of a period in which good conduct is presumed, and this is a practice by which the state of the penitent is judged across the four seasons, which reveal natures.

Since their exception was from the rejection of testimony and from being called sinful, the sense is: accept their testimony and do not describe them as sinners. He gave the reason with His saying, ﴿indeed Allah﴾, meaning the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿is Forgiving﴾, meaning He covers over for them what they committed because they turned back from it, ﴿Merciful﴾, meaning He treats them with honour in the manner of a merciful one toward the one he shows mercy to, by accepting their testimony.

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 6:

Since the word *al-muhsanat* (chaste women) is general and includes wives, and since they have a ruling different from what came before, He excluded them by His saying: ﴿And those who accuse﴾, that is, of fornication, ﴿their wives﴾, that is, from among the believing free women, the slave women, and the disbelieving women, ﴿and have no witnesses for them except themselves﴾. This implies that if the husband is one of the four, it suffices. However, this implication is refuted by the fact that the verse is a narration of an incident in which there were no witnesses. Its preceding verse, ﴿then they do not produce four witnesses﴾ [al-Nur: 4], requires that the witnesses be other than the accuser. Perhaps He excluded him from the witnesses because his *li'an* (sworn mutual imprecation between spouses) takes the form of the wording of testimony. The school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, holds that his testimony is not accepted against his wife in this matter. Ibn al-Rif'a said in *al-Kifaya*: for two reasons. The first is that fornication affects the place of the husband's right, since the fornicator enjoys the benefits that are due to him. So his testimony about its attribute includes proving a wrong done by another to what is owed to him, and therefore it is not heard, just as when he testifies that someone harmed his slave. The second is that whoever testifies to his wife's adultery, the very act of his testimony indicates the display of enmity, because her adultery troubles his heart by soiling his bed and bringing shame upon him and upon his child. This is more intense in enmity than painful beating or vile insult. Al-Qadi al-Husayn said: it is to this cause that al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, pointed, and it is the one that al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib related in the chapter on the penalty for the highway robber from Shaykh Abu Hamid.

﴿So the testimony of one of them﴾, that is, against the one who accused her, ﴿is four testimonies﴾ from five, in place of four witnesses, ﴿by Allah﴾, that is, joined with this noble and greatest Name, which necessitates the summoning of all the attributes of majesty and beauty, ﴿that he is surely among the truthful﴾, that is, in what he accused her of.

The fifth [oath]: that the curse of Allah [be upon him] — i.e., the Supreme King — ﴿upon him﴾, i.e., upon this slanderer himself, ﴿if he is among the liars﴾ regarding what he accused her of. And because he has, by these solemn oaths, made certain of his truthfulness and of Allah's judgment for his acquittal, paternity is negated from him, and from its negation follows the everlasting separation without any pronouncement, since she is not fit to be a bed (firash) for him, for the child belongs to the bed (al-walad lil-firash) [the legal husband]. The li'an is not valid except before a judge (hakim). There is no concealing how this distances [the husband] from slander, by requiring greater caution, because of the repetition in it, the association of the Greatest Name, the combining of an affirmation with what implies a negation, and the invocation of a curse that removes one from the attribute of the believer. So when the husband does this, the punishment of the slander penalty (hadd al-qadhf) falls from him, and it becomes obligatory upon the accused woman. For this reason the Exalted said.

"And it averts from her the punishment" — i.e., it removes (yadfa'u) from her, the woman accused (al-maqdhufa), the punishment (al-'adhab), i.e., the well-known one, which is the prescribed penalty (al-hadd) that the preceding testimony of the husband had made obligatory upon her: "that she bear witness with four testimonies" — out of five — "by Allah," the One to whom belong all the most beautiful Names and the lofty attributes, as was mentioned earlier concerning the husband, "that he is surely among the liars" in what he said about her.

﴿Al-khamisah﴾ (the fifth) of the testimonies: ﴿that the wrath of Allah﴾, to whom belongs all command, so that there is no equal to Him, ﴿be upon her﴾. This is stronger than the curse (al-la'n), which is expulsion, because expulsion may come for a reason other than wrath. The reason for the severity against her is to urge her to confess the truth, since the husband is supported by the indication that he would not undertake the exposure of his own family, which entails exposure of himself, unless he were truthful. It is also because she is the source of corruption, the one who tears away the veil, and the one who mixes lineages. ﴿If he was﴾, that is, as a firm state, ﴿of the truthful﴾, that is, in what he accused her of.

Al-Bukhari in the Tafsir (commentary) section and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and others, may Allah be pleased with them, that [p. 219] Hilal ibn Umayyah, may Allah be pleased with him, accused his wife before the Prophet ﷺ of [adultery] with Shurayk ibn Sahma', may Allah be pleased with him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Produce evidence, or else a punishment upon your back." He said: "O Messenger of Allah! If one of us sees a man upon his wife, must he go out seeking evidence?" The Prophet ﷺ kept saying: "Evidence, or else a punishment upon your back." Hilal said: "By the One who sent you with the truth! Indeed I am truthful, and Allah will surely send down something that clears my back from the punishment." Then Jibril, peace be upon him, descended and revealed upon him: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ [al-Nur: 6], and he recited until he reached ﴿if he is of the truthful﴾. The Prophet ﷺ then turned away and sent for them both. Hilal came and testified, while the Prophet ﷺ was saying: "Indeed Allah knows that one of you two is a liar. Will any of you repent?" Then she stood and testified. When she reached the fifth, they stopped her and said: "Indeed it will bring about [her damnation]." She hesitated and drew back until we thought she would retract, then she said: "I will not disgrace my people for the rest of the day." So she went on, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Watch her. If she brings forth a child with dark eyes, large buttocks, and thick calves, then it belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'." She brought it forth in that manner, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Had it not been for what has preceded from the Book of Allah, there would have been a matter between me and her."

Al-Bukhari also narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him, that the occasion of its revelation was a story like this one, concerning 'Uwaymir. It has already been mentioned that there is no impediment to a single verse having several occasions of revelation, together or at different times. [p. 220]

When God, exalted is He, forbade by these sentences the violation of honour and lineage, and thereby protected lives and property, the (implied) estimate is known to be: "Had it not been that He, exalted is He, is the best of forgivers and the best of the merciful, He would not have done this to you, and He would have exposed the sinners and revealed the secrets of the frivolous. The order would have collapsed, and you would have settled into laxity regarding the rulings." So He joined to this implied estimate His words: ﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy﴾, that is, by what He possesses of generosity and beauty and characterization with the attributes of perfection, ﴿upon you and His mercy﴾, that is, toward you, ﴿and that God﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in knowledge and power, ﴿is Oft-Returning﴾, that is, One who turns back the disobedient to Himself, ﴿Wise﴾, who governs affairs and so restrains them from corruption by what He knows of their consequences, so as not to expose every disobedient person. He did not require four witnesses, as a covering for you, and He would have ordered his punishment with what his disobedience requires, and your order would have been corrupted and your binding and loosening would have fallen into disorder. And the like of this, whose description cannot be reached, so that the soul goes off in every direction concerning it. Thus, as they say: "An unspoken matter is more eloquent than a spoken one."

Then he gave the reason for what "law lawla" (had it not been) implied, such as "but He did not do that out of His bounty and mercy toward you," by His words, emphatically, given what he knew of the state of many who became angry for the sake of God and His Messenger, desiring to punish the slanderers by cutting off their necks. He thus alerted them that this would lead to a great corruption: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander﴾ (p-221), that is, the worst of lies, because it is speech diverted from its meaning to its opposite, turned from its face to its back. It was defined (with *al-*) to add to its ugliness in this context, to the point that it seems there is no slander but this one, because it concerned the Mother of the Believers, Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who was among the people most deserving of praise for her chastity, nobility, purity and generosity. Whoever accused her of evil had turned the matter from its best face to its ugliest back. He left out naming her, to exalt her above this position and to keep the sanctity of her lofty side far from this aim. ﴿A band﴾, that is, a group, at least ten and at most forty. Because they are a band, some of them protect others, so their affair becomes strong, since the core of the root *ʿ-ṣ-b* (ʿaṣaba) is strength. And they are, despite that, ﴿among you﴾, that is, among those who are counted among the Muslims in your reckoning. Had God exposed them in all that they concealed and proclaimed, and commanded you to punish them with what they deserve, the bonds among you would have been corrupted, through their protecting themselves, for they were many, and the partisanship of their friends for them, unless by a supernatural matter that would preserve from this, as experience revealed when the Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon and said: "Who will excuse me regarding a man whose harm has reached my family?" when they nearly fought one another, were it not that the Prophet ﷺ calmed them (p-222). God, in His mercy toward you, prevents their plotting by clarifying their lie, and in His wisdom He conceals them and frightens them, so that the root of their scheming is cut off and the causes of their harm are severed.

Since this required concern for their affair, He followed it with His words, belittling their matter, addressing the sincere believers, and in particular the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Aisha and her mother, and Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, may God be pleased with them: ﴿Do not think it bad for you﴾, that is, the slander, ﴿bad for you﴾, O believers, that someone might believe it or that discord might arise from it. ﴿Rather, it is good for you﴾ through the establishment of innocence, which brings a lasting honor that is not reached, through its recitation across the ages by the tongues of countless servants in most lands, and through the consolation of the Messenger ﷺ and the truthful ones by this, together with abundant reward for patience over the bitterness of this talk, and through the confirmation of the miraculousness of the Qur'an, beyond its miraculousness in eloquence, by its truthfulness in preserving the one whom it praised in that long age that she lived with the Messenger of God ﷺ and after him until she died, may God the Most High be pleased with her, the most pious of people in religion, the most evidently chaste, the purest in honor, and the most pure in soul. So it is a truthful tongue in this world and an elevation of ranks in the Hereafter, along with other wisdoms that the Creator of souls arranged, including religious benefits, rulings and etiquettes (p-223).

Since nothing heals a person's anger more than the victory of the King, the Judge, for him, He gave the reason for this by His words: ﴿For every man among them﴾, that is, of the slanderers, ﴿is what﴾, that is, the recompense of what ﴿he has earned﴾ by his plunging into it, ﴿of sin﴾, which brings about his misery. The form *ifti'al* from *kasaba* is used for sin, indicating that sin is incurred through what one undertakes with firm resolve and strong intention, which the action confirms with its seriousness and energy. And it is used for good deeds in the sense of mere effort, indicating that reward is written by the mere doing of good, indeed even by its intention. ﴿And he who took upon himself the greater part of it﴾, that is, its main share, by spreading it and proclaiming it, ﴿among them, for him﴾, in what belongs to him, because of his excessive harm, ﴿is a great punishment﴾, that is, greater than the punishment of the rest, because they said nothing except that its like of burden fell upon him, without that diminishing anything of their burdens. The story of the slander is well known in the Sahih and the Sunan and elsewhere, and is very famous. It is that the Prophet ﷺ went out on the campaign against Banu al-Mustaliq after the verse of hijab (the veil) had been revealed, and with him was al-Siddiqa, daughter of al-Siddiq, his wife, Mother of the Believers Aisha, may God the Most High be pleased with her, who was riding in her howdah. She lost a necklace of hers one night, so she returned to the place where she had relieved herself (p-224) and searched for it. The Prophet ﷺ set out, and her camel-drivers lifted her howdah and loaded it, thinking she was in it. When she returned and found no one, she lay down in the place of her howdah, hoping they would realize she was missing and come back. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, may God be pleased with him, had stayed behind the army, and he arrived at their place in the morning. When he saw her, and he had used to see her before the hijab, he said "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" and made his mount kneel, and her hand was trampled under it. He spoke no word except his recitation. The Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, mounted, and he set off with her until he caught up with the army while they were resting at midday. The people of the slander spoke about the two of them, may God be pleased with both of them. Among those named were Abd Allah ibn Ubayy the hypocrite, Zayd ibn Rifa'ah, Mistah ibn Uthathah, Hamnah bint Jahsh, and Hassan ibn Thabit." Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: "Among other people whose names I do not know, except that they were a band, as God the Most High said."

Thus they mentioned Hassan among them. By God, I do not at all suspect him, even if his naming came in the Sahih, for the trustworthy may err for countless reasons, as one knows who has practiced the criticism of reports. How could it be supposed of him, when his only occupation was praising the Prophet ﷺ, defending him, and disparaging his enemies? The Messenger of God ﷺ testified that Gabriel, peace be upon him, was with him. So I swear by God that the One who strengthened him with Gabriel would not have left him to himself in such an incident. The memorizer ʿImad al-Din ibn Kathir al-Dimashqi, may God have mercy on him, had preceded me in defending him. And how could he not defend him when he is the one who said:

*My father and his father, and my honor,*
*are a shield for the honor of Muhammad from you.*

And he is the one who praised Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and denied what was attributed to him:

*Chaste and dignified, she is never accused of doubt,*
*and she wakes up empty of the flesh of the heedless.*

*The beloved of the best of people in religion and lineage,*
*the Prophet of guidance and the abundant noble deeds.*

*The noble lady of a tribe of Luayy ibn Ghalib,*
*whose noble efforts and glory do not decline.*

*Refined, God has perfumed her tent*
*and purified her from every blemish and falsehood.*

*If what you conveyed from me was what I said,*
*then may my fingers never raise my whip to me.*

*And how, when my love and support while I live*
*are for the family of the Messenger of God, the adornment of gatherings?*

*For him are ranks high above people, whose excellence*
*the rush of the boaster falls short of reaching.*

And the Hafiz Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr said in *al-Istiab*: "A people denied that Hassan had plunged into the slander and was flogged for it, and they related from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she cleared him of it." End.

The people of the slander continued in this for more than a month, while God the Most High knows what they say, and that their talk nearly cuts the livers of the dearest of His creatures to Him. He is capable of refuting them at the very first moment they plunged into it, but He, glory be to Him, willed for some people the raising of ranks, and for others destruction. Alas, what the Prophet ﷺ, the Truthful one, and his family, may God be pleased with them, and everyone who loved them met, and they are the best of people! God, glory be to Him and exalted, gives respite to the slanderers and allows them time. By my life, the situation is as Abu Tammam al-Ta'i said in a qasida:

*Thus let the matter be grave and the affair be weighty,*
*for there is no excuse for an eye whose water has not flowed.*

When Aisha, may God be pleased with her, heard the words of the people of the slander, she fell unconscious, and a fever with shivering struck her. She asked the Messenger of God ﷺ for permission to go to her father's house, and he permitted her. She asked her mother about the news, and her mother informed her. She wept and sobbed. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was in an upper room reciting, and he heard her sound, so he came down and asked her mother. She said: "What he mentioned about her affair has reached her." His eyes overflowed. She, may God be pleased with her, continued weeping until she thought that weeping would split her liver. An Ansari woman, of those with fidelity, comfort, generosity, selflessness, and noble character, helped her in weeping, so she wept with her. "The Messenger of God ﷺ asked about Aisha, may God be pleased with her, from her servant-girl Barirah, may God be pleased with her, and she was appalled that he might suspect such a thing of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, so she said: 'Glory be to God! By God, I know nothing of her except what the goldsmith knows of the red gold ingot.' The Messenger of God ﷺ addressed the people from the pulpit and sought his excuse from whoever had spoken about his family, though he knew nothing of them but good. The Messenger of God ﷺ, who is the truthful and the one whose truthfulness is confirmed, bore witness to the righteousness of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, may God be pleased with him, and that he knew nothing of him but good. The people nearly fought one another, and the Messenger of God ﷺ calmed them. Then, after he had prayed the afternoon prayer, he entered upon Aisha, may God be pleased with her, while she was weeping and the Ansari woman was with her. He admonished her, and she replied and replied well. God revealed to the Messenger of God ﷺ in that gathering, and he was seized by what used to seize him of distress." Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "As for me, when I saw what I saw, by God, I was not frightened nor did I care. I knew that I was innocent and that God does not wrong me. As for my parents, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Aisha! The Messenger of God ﷺ was not relieved until I thought their souls would leave them, out of fear that God would bring about the fulfillment of what the people had said." She said: "Then it was lifted from him, and I saw the joy in his face, as he wiped the sweat from his forehead and said: 'Rejoice, O Aisha, for God has revealed your innocence.' I was at my most angry, and my parents said to me: 'Stand up to him!' I said: 'By God, I will not stand up to him, nor will I praise him, nor praise you both, but I praise only God, who revealed my innocence. You heard it, and you did not deny it, nor did you change it.'" And God the Most High revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander﴾, the ten verses in full. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "By God, the man who was accused said: 'Glory be to God! By Him in whose hand is my soul, I have never uncovered the veil of any woman.'" She said: "Then he was killed afterward as a martyr in the way of God." End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 12:

When He, glorified and exalted is He, had informed them of their punishment, and among the believers there were those who heard it and remained silent, while among them there were those who heard it and spoke of it in amazement at the one who had uttered it, or seeking confirmation of the matter, and among them were those who denied it, He, glorified is He, followed it with a rebuke of them, in the manner of their address, praising those who denied it. So He said, resuming with an exhortation: ﴿Why, when you heard it﴾, that is, why did you not, why did you not do so, ﴿when you heard it﴾, O you who claim faith? And since this slander had been concocted by men and women together, He said: ﴿the believing men and the believing women thought well﴾, that is, of their own kind, ﴿of themselves﴾, that is, of one another, ﴿good﴾. The original form would have been "you thought," but He turned to the third person as a warning of reproach, and He explicitly mentioned the women, and drew attention to the quality that calls for thinking well, as a frightening of the one who thought ill, lest he suffer an evil end. ﴿Of themselves﴾ in truth, ﴿good﴾, while they were not those about whom it was spoken, so they affirmed her innocence, because a person does not think ill of people except what he himself is characterized by, or of his brethren, since the believers are like one body, or they thought (p-229) what would be thought of a man if he were alone with his mother, and of a woman if she were alone with her son, since the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are the mothers of the believers. ﴿And they said: This is a manifest lie﴾, that is, a great falsehood, a fabrication lying upon its face, ﴿manifest﴾, that is, clear in itself, making clear to others. Its clarity and evidentness is that the one who harbours doubt almost says: "Take me," for he strives to conceal himself with all his effort. Thus the bringing of Safwan with 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, riding upon his camel, leading her into the army in the middle of the day, while all the people were witnessing and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among them, the revelation descending upon him, out of confidence in the goodness of his deed, heedless of what the people of doubt would think of him, is the strongest proof of innocence and of the lie of the slanderers. Had there been even the slightest suspicion, each of the two would have come alone, in a manner of concealment and fear by which his treachery would have been recognized. Matters are tested by their outcome, and a person thinks of people only what is in himself. Abu Ayyub al-Ansari and his wife, may Allah be pleased with them both, acted in accordance with what this verse indicates. Ibn Ishaq said: My father Ishaq ibn Yasar related to me from some men of the Banu al-Najjar that Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with him, was told by his wife Umm Ayyub: "O Abu Ayyub, do you not hear what the people are saying about 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her?" He said: "Yes, and that is a lie. Would you have done such a thing, O Umm Ayyub?" She said: "No, by Allah, I would not have done it." He said: "Then 'Aisha, by Allah, is better than you." And al-Baghawi narrated that he said: "Glory be to You, this is a tremendous slander," and the verse was revealed in accordance with his statement, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then the Exalted (subḥānahu) gave a reason for the demonstration of the liars' falsehood, saying, rebuking those who fabricated it and spread it, and instructing those whom He urged to think well (of their brethren): ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ That is, "Why did they not do so? Why not?" ﴿They﴾ — that is, the slanderers who fabricated it at first — ﴿for it﴾ — if they were truthful — ﴿with four witnesses﴾, as was previously stated, that slander is not permitted except with them.

And since their lying was a consequence of their not bringing the witnesses, He said: ﴿Then, since they did not bring the witnesses﴾ — that is, when they did not bring the described witnesses — ﴿then those﴾ — that is, the far removed from what is right — ﴿with Allah﴾ — that is, in the judgment of the Supreme King, and in this particular incident specifically in His knowledge — ﴿they are the liars﴾, that is, the great lie, outwardly and inwardly.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 14:

When he had shown them, by establishing proof, that the ones who plunged into this matter (al-kha'ideen) were lying, and that they deserved blame, and this was an encouragement for the people of taqwa (God-consciousness), he showed that they deserved, through their negligence in denouncing it, a general retribution (al-intiqam), in a context that gives glad tidings of pardon. He said, conjoining it to the preceding ﴿wa-lawla﴾ (and were it not): ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah﴾, i.e., the One encompassing the attributes of perfection, ﴿upon you, and His mercy﴾, i.e., His dealing with you with abundant bounty, looking to grace and honor, which necessarily accompanies mercy, ﴿in this world﴾ by accepting repentance and dealing with you with forbearance, ﴿and the Hereafter﴾ by pardoning whoever among you He wills to pardon, ﴿would have touched you﴾, i.e., swiftly and generally, ﴿for what you plunged into﴾, i.e., you rushed into it in whatever manner it was, ﴿therein﴾, some of you literally and some of you figuratively through not denouncing it, ﴿a great punishment﴾, i.e., (p-231) one before which blame and flogging are considered trivial, by which one would perish, and the punishment of the Hereafter would be joined to it.

Then he explained the time of its occurrence and the moment of its swift arrival by saying: ﴿When﴾, that is, when you [were] receiving it, ﴿you were receiving it﴾, that is, striving to receive, i.e., to accept this obscene talk and to pass it on, ﴿with your tongues﴾, by spreading it among some, asking others, and remaining silent among others. ﴿And saying﴾ — and His saying ﴿with your mouths﴾ is a depiction of its extreme ugliness and an indication that it is a saying with no reality to it, so it cannot be impressed upon the heart with any kind of proof. He emphasized this meaning by saying: ﴿about which you have no knowledge﴾, that is, in any respect whatsoever, and its indefiniteness is for belittlement. ﴿And you considered it﴾, as evidenced by your silence about denouncing it, ﴿a trivial matter, while it is﴾, that is, while the state is that it is, ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾, that is, of the One whose greatness no one can reach the measure of, ﴿a grave matter﴾, that is, in and of itself; and even if it were said about someone other than the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, how much more so when it is directed at her sanctified honour, she being the wife of the Seal of the Prophets and Imam of the Messengers, upon him be the best of blessings and the best of peace.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 16:

When He had made clear its vileness and abomination, and its ugliness and enormity, He followed the first admonition in His words ﴿Why did you not, when you heard it,﴾ [al-Nur: 12] with a second admonition, saying: ﴿And why not, when you heard it,﴾ meaning: "Why did you not, at the moment you heard it, say—﴿you should have said﴾, meaning: at the time of hearing it, without hesitation or stammering." He placed a separation between the particle of reproach (ta'dib, rebuke) and the statement being rebuked by means of the adverbial phrase, because adverbial expressions place a thing in the position of itself, since it occurs within them, and they are inseparable from it. [Also,] mentioning it (the adverbial phrase) alerts to the importance of it, because it is obligatory to hasten to what is being reproached: ﴿It is not for us﴾, meaning: it is not befitting or proper for us, ﴿to speak of this﴾, literally by utterance, nor figuratively by remaining silent about denouncing it, ﴿this﴾, meaning: the like of it, regarding even the lowest of people; so how much more regarding one whom the All-Knowing, All-Wise chose for the companionship of the most perfect of creation. Then you showed the intensity of your aversion to it by joining this negation with your words: ﴿Glory be to You!﴾, in wonder that such a thing should occur to the mind in any circumstance whatsoever.

Since glorifying Allah Most High in such a situation, even though it is an expression of wonder, points to a great exaltation of the station in which the wonder occurred, it was fitting to connect with it, as a reason for the wonder and the negation, His words: ﴿This is a great calumny﴾, meaning: a lie that stuns whoever is confronted with it and bewilders him, because of the severity of its effect upon the inner faculties, since he is in the utmost heedlessness of it, being the furthest of people from it. Then He magnified it by His words: ﴿great﴾. The intended meaning is that what befits a person first is not to think ill of his believing brothers and sisters, and to hear nothing about them but good. If Satan overcomes him and some of that imagery is imprinted upon his mind, then he should not speak of it, and should hasten to deny it.

Since all of this is admonition and correction for them, He addressed it with His words: ﴿Allah admonishes you﴾, meaning: He softens your hearts, He to whom belongs all perfection, so He grants respite out of His forbearance and does not hasten out of His wisdom and knowledge, by warning in a manner of gentle appeal: ﴿that you never return to the like of it﴾, meaning: out of aversion to your returning to it (p-233), ﴿as long as you are fit to hear this statement.﴾ Then He magnified this admonition and set alight the one who hears it with His words: ﴿if you are believers﴾, meaning: characterized by faith and firmly established in it, for then you would not return. But if you return, then you are not truthful in your claim to be characterized by it.

Allah makes clear to you the signs (Allah makes clear to you the signs), ﴿ويُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ﴾ meaning, by virtue of His being characterized by the attributes of majesty and generosity. ﴿لَكُمُ الآياتِ﴾ means the indications that clarify the truth and falsehood, concerning every religious or worldly matter. ﴿واللَّهُ﴾ meaning, the One encompassing all perfection, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ so trust His explanation. ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ He does not place anything except in its most fitting place, even if its understanding is difficult for you. So do not hesitate concerning any of His commands. And know that He did not choose for His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, except the sincere ones among His servants, according to their ranks with Him and their nearness to his heart.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 19:**

Since one of the greatest forms of admonition is explaining the punishment deserved for sin, He disciplined them with a third discipline, more severe than the first two. So He said, admonishing and condemning the state of those who engage in the slander (ifk), and warning and threatening them: ﴿Indeed, those who love﴾. He expressed it with "love" to indicate that no one commits this, with its enormity, except one who loves it, and no one loves it except one far removed from uprightness (istiqamah). ﴿That indecency should spread﴾, meaning that it be disseminated by speech or by action. ﴿Indecency﴾, meaning the grave act of great ugliness, and that it should acquire a faction (shi'ah) who defend it, (p-٢٣٤) ﴿among those who believe﴾, even if they are at the lowest levels of faith, so how much more so for one who has ascended its peak and reached its utmost limit. ﴿For them is a painful punishment﴾, as a deterrent against their desire to spread the like of this, because of its great harm. ﴿In this world﴾, by the prescribed punishment (hadd) and other means by which God takes vengeance upon them, ﴿and the Hereafter﴾, for God knows whether the hadd has expiated for them all of their transgression or not. ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning the One who combines the attributes of majesty and beauty, ﴿knows﴾, meaning He has complete knowledge. He knows the measures of things, what has appeared of them and what has been concealed, and what the wisdom is in concealing them or revealing them, or otherwise, of all matters. ﴿And you do not know﴾, meaning you have no knowledge of yourselves, so act upon what Allah has taught you, and do not transgress it, lest you go astray.

When he concluded with the judgment against them for ignorance, and the implied sense, as indicated by what follows in the conjunction without an antecedent, was: "Had it not been for God's grace upon you and His mercy toward you, He would have hastened the destruction of the wrongdoers, since such conduct had spread, with a worldly punishment that would be joined to the punishment of the Hereafter." He then conjoined to this his saying, repeating the reminder of the favor of His postponing hastened punishment and omitting the response, so that the repetition and the omission would signal the intensity of the emphasis and the severity of the awe: ﴿And had it not been for God's grace upon you﴾, that is, the One who possesses all majesty and honor, ﴿and His mercy toward you﴾, ﴿and that﴾, that is, had it not been that ﴿God﴾, that is, the One who has complete power, so that His mercy outweighed His wrath, ﴿is Kind﴾ toward you, in establishing what removes your ignorance and what guards your inner states through sending messengers, sending down scriptures, and establishing limits that deter from ignorance and lead to piety, which is the fruit of knowledge. For kindness (al-ra'fah), as was previously explained concerning the pilgrimage and elsewhere, raises up the one toward whom it is shown, because it is the gentlest and most intense form of mercy, and it proceeds upon the most upright paths, so that by its course it guards in secret the appearance of what would call for pardon. Sometimes this guarding occurs through potential, by establishing proofs, and sometimes it is joined to that action by creating guidance in the heart, through the connection the one shown kindness has to ease of submission and strength of readiness. ﴿And Merciful﴾ through what He grants you of ranks, in return for the fruits of that guarding, namely the pleasing deeds He has bestowed upon you. The response is omitted, and its estimated sense is: "He would have left you in the darkness of ignorance, wandering blindly. Then strife would have erupted among you until you destroyed one another and reached everlasting punishment after lasting distress."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 21:

When He had informed them that He had not sent down this law to them through this compassionate and merciful Messenger except as a mercy to them, after warning them against the sources of ignorance, He forbade them from persisting in it, in a context that makes known that the one who calls to it is the enemy, Satan. So He said, addressing them with the call to attention, gladdening them: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning, those who have affirmed faith, ﴿do not follow﴾, meaning, with your effort, ﴿the footsteps﴾, meaning the path, ﴿of Satan﴾, meaning do not emulate him or take the ways he leads you to take by adorning them, in any matter whatsoever. It seems that by the form of the verb (ittifa'ala, "to follow") he indicated pardon for lapses.

Since the implied sense is: whoever turns aside from his path comes to what is good and right, He joined to it His saying: ﴿And whoever follows﴾, meaning with firm resolve, not by way of error or forgetfulness. He made it explicit and did not use a pronoun, for greater deterrence, so He said: ﴿the footsteps of Satan﴾, meaning, and whoever emulates him falls into the pits of ignorance that give rise to every evil. ﴿For indeed he﴾, meaning Satan, ﴿enjoins immorality﴾, which is what is extremely ugly, ﴿and wrongdoing﴾, which is what the Law has not permitted. He first aims at the highest levels of error, and if he does not attain it, he descends to its lowest levels, and perhaps he proceeds by other than this. It is known that whoever follows one whose way is this acts by his deed and becomes in the utmost lowliness. This is more intensely deterrent than returning the pronoun in "for indeed he" to "whoever". And God is the Granter of success.

Since the implied sense is: were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan despite his commanding of vile things, He joined to it His saying: ﴿And were it not for the grace of God﴾, meaning the Lord of Majesty and Honour, ﴿upon you﴾, meaning by purifying your souls and elevating them from the lowly things they crave to the lofty ones, ﴿and His mercy﴾ toward you by honouring you and raising your rank through the law of repentance that expiates what ignorance drew you into of deficient speech and base deeds, ﴿none of you would ever have been purified﴾, meaning would have become pure and grown. He emphasized the comprehensiveness with His saying: ﴿of anyone﴾, and generalized the time with His saying: ﴿ever. But God﴾, meaning by His majesty and perfection, ﴿purifies﴾, meaning cleanses and causes to grow, ﴿whom He wills﴾ of His servants, from all the defilements of the self and the diseases of the heart. Although the servants and their characters are so widespread and numerous that none but Him can count them, He purified among you whom He willed and preserved him from this calumny, and abandoned whom He willed.

Then He concluded the verse with what purification cannot be valid without, saying: ﴿And God﴾, meaning He to whom belong all attributes of perfection, ﴿is Hearing﴾, meaning of all their words, ﴿Knowing﴾ of everything that occurs to their minds and arises from their states and actions. So He is aware of who is fit for purification and who is not. Thank God for His purifying you from plunging into what others have plunged into, whom He abandoned to some degree of abandonment; be patient with them in that, and do not cut off your kindness from them, for that will be an increase in your purity and a means of drawing toward faith whoever among them He knows to have good in him, so that his repentance is accepted and his sin is washed away. This is what is meant (p-238) by His saying.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 22:

﴿And let not those of virtue among you⁠—﴾ i.e., those who swear emphatically in oath⁠—﴿and abundance⁠﴾ [the ones whom I made, by the knowledge and good character I gave them, worthy of the righteousness of others] ﴿and abundance﴾ i.e., by what I have bestowed upon them of worldly provision.

Since the context (al-siyaq), the sequence (al-sibaq) and what follows (al-lihaq) make the meaning clear, there was no need to mention the particle of negation, so He said: ﴿that they should not give﴾. Then He mentioned the attributes that call for beneficence, saying: ﴿to those near of kin﴾. He enumerated them with the particle of conjunction to multiply them and to magnify their matter, and to point out that one of them is sufficient for beneficence, so how much more when they are combined! Then He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and the needy﴾, i.e., those who do not find what suffices them even if they have no kinship, ﴿and the emigrants﴾ from their families, homes and wealth, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, i.e., the One whose bounty encompasses all creatures, owing to His all-encompassing majesty and generosity, even if the first two attributes are absent from them. For these attributes indicate that they are among those whom Allah has purified. Enumerating them, by making them the reason for pardon, is evidence that one who is purified among non-infallible persons may slip, and purification overtakes him through repentance, so he returns as he was. The three may also be for one described person, because the occasion of its revelation was Mistah, may Allah be pleased with him; so the conjunction here is for the firm establishment of each attribute among them.

Since the prohibition of that was not explicit regarding pardon, and the implied meaning was: "let them give to them," He connected to it, explicitly stating the intended meaning, His saying: ﴿and let them pardon﴾, i.e., pardon their slip by erasing it and covering it with the veils of forbearance that they draw over it, until no trace of it remains. And since erasure does not negate remembrance, He said: ﴿and let them overlook﴾, i.e., turn away from it entirely and altogether, so that they do not bring it to mind, so that this produces beneficence. From this comes "al-Safuh," which is the generous one.

Since the sweetness of address causes every rebuke to be forgotten, He, glorified is He, turned with His grace, bounty and favor toward those of virtue, encouraging them to do to others what they love to be done to them, and warning them against being harsh toward them if they were harsh, saying: ﴿Do you not love﴾, i.e., O people of virtue, ﴿that Allah should forgive﴾, i.e., the Greatest King, ﴿you﴾, i.e., what you have fallen short of in His right. The occasion of its revelation, as in the Sahih from the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, was that her father, may Allah be pleased with him, had sworn after Allah had cleared 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that he would not spend on Mistah ibn Uthatha, his maternal cousin, because he had engaged in the slander of the people of the lie. In the tafsir of al-Isfahani, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them: some of the Companions, among them Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them, swore that they would not give charity to a man who had spoken something of the slander and would not benefit him, so Allah revealed this verse.

And what greater proof is needed of the honor of al-Siddiq than Allah's testimony, majestic is His majesty, that he is among those of virtue! How noble is such honor, how lofty! And how exalted is such nobility and pride! Especially since he, may Allah be pleased with him, confirmed it by pardoning the one who spoke ill of the fruit of his heart and the essence of his liver, namely al-Siddiqa, the wife of the Seal of the Messengers and the best of all creation, and by swearing that he would never cut off support from him. Glory be to Allah, what radiant character! And what pure, pious and noble dispositions, most exalted and loftiest!

Since the answer was decisive, as al-Siddiq answered: "Yes, by Allah! We love that Allah should forgive us," and it was as if it had been said: "So forgive those who wronged you, for Allah is a just Judge who recompenses their wrong to you if He wills, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Appreciative, who appreciates what you have done for them," He connected to it His saying: ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., together with His perfect power and all-encompassing knowledge, ﴿is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. From His attribute is that: if He wills, He forgives your sins by erasing them so that no trace remains, and has mercy on you after their erasure by bestowing favor upon you as you did with them, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

(p-241) When the closing of the verse with these two attributes, after the command to pardon, might embolden someone toward a transgression like this, he connected to it, warning against falling into the like of that, his saying, generalizing the ruling: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse﴾, that is, of unchastity, ﴿chaste women﴾, that is, those who have made themselves, in their chastity, like a fortress.

When the one who intends an evil deed and undertakes it knows what he is accusing them of, placing it before his eyes, he emphasized the meaning of chastity with his saying: ﴿heedless﴾, that is, of wrongdoing, to the point of not even mentioning it. And since the attribute of faith carries one to every good and prevents every evil, he alerted that what drives one to the two preceding attributes is only God-consciousness (taqwa), and he directed what they possess of discernment toward what God has over them of rights, so he said: ﴿believing﴾.

When these attributes established distance from evil, he mentioned the penalty of the slanderer, restraining him and warning against him, in the passive form, because what is feared is the curse and not the specific person who is cursed, and to alert that the curse falls upon everyone from whom it is possible. So he said: ﴿They are cursed﴾, that is, they are removed far from God's mercy, and they are treated with the treatment of one removed from the prescribed punishment (hadd) and other matters, ﴿in this world and the Hereafter﴾. Then he increased the magnitude of the slander against one whose attributes are these, so he said: ﴿And for them﴾, that is, in the Hereafter, ﴿is a great punishment﴾. He restricted it with the attribute of faith because slandering a disbelieving woman, although forbidden, does not include this whole combination. And this ruling, although general, is primarily and principally for the sake of the Siddiqa (the truthful one), and in its severity, of a kind rarely found in the Qur'an, in its announcement that elevates her station, manifests her matter, and displays her great honor, is something that exceeds description.

Then He followed this with mention of the day on which the consequence of that will occur, in a manner that added greater magnitude to the matter, so He said: ﴿On the day when their tongues, and their hands and their feet, will testify against them﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, in that great assembly, ﴿their tongues﴾ if they refrain from lying, ﴿and their hands and their feet﴾ if their tongues deny falsehood and wickedness, thinking that lying will benefit them, ﴿concerning what they used to do﴾ of this slander and other than it.

Then He intensified the awe with His saying: ﴿On that day﴾, i.e., when these limbs bear witness against them, ﴿Allah will pay them in full﴾, i.e., the One who encompasses everything in knowledge and power, and to Him belongs all perfection, ﴿their due recompense﴾, i.e., their requital, ﴿the truth﴾, i.e., that which becomes manifest to everyone among the people of that great gathering, that they truly deserve it, so that no one is able to raise any kind of objection to it. ﴿And they will know﴾, i.e., at that time, due to the severing of all means and the lifting of every veil, ﴿that Allah﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs absolute greatness, so that there is no equal to Him, ﴿He is﴾, i.e., He alone, ﴿the Truth﴾, i.e., the One whose command is established, so that there is no command for anyone other than Him,

﴿the Manifest﴾: the One than whom nothing is more evident regarding His divinity, His knowledge, His power, His being singular in all attributes of perfection, and His being exalted above all marks of deficiency. Thus they will regret (p-243) what they did in the world of things that impair vigilance and to which heedlessness applies. Ibn Kathir said: The Mothers of the Believers are more worthy of entering into this than any chaste woman, especially she who was the cause of the revelation, namely ʿĀʾishah, daughter of aṣ-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with them both. The scholars have unanimously agreed that whoever reviles her after this, and accuses her of what was alleged after what is mentioned in this verse, then he is a disbeliever, because he is contradicting the Qur'an. Regarding the rest of the Mothers of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with them, there are two opinions, the more correct of which is that they are like her. And Allah knows best. – End of quote.

It is known from these verses and what precedes them from the beginning of the surah and what follows them to its end that Allah, the Exalted, did not make severe any of the sins as severe as the matter of the slander (al-ifk), nor did He threaten for anything what He threatened for it, and He emphasized, reproached, rebuked and censured, all of this to manifest the nobility of His Messenger ﷺ, to be jealous on his behalf, to magnify the sanctity of his honour, and to safeguard his veil.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 26:

When the verse contained His description, exalted is He, of His knowledge of hidden things, it followed it with what serves as the rationale for the verse ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾ [al-Nur: 3], as an observed proof of the innocence of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her. He said: ﴿The evil women﴾, meaning from among the women, and He placed this attribute first because their speech was about her. So when it is negated, goodness is established. ﴿For evil men﴾, meaning from among the men. Since it could not be understood from this that evil is restricted to evil women, He said: ﴿And evil men﴾, meaning from among the men also, ﴿are for evil women﴾, meaning from among the women.

When this produced her innocence, may Allah be pleased with her, because she is the consort of the best of creation, He affirmed it with His saying: ﴿And good women﴾, meaning from among them, ﴿are for good men﴾, meaning from among them, ﴿and good men are for good women.﴾ By this, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, decreed that every kind joins its like and does the deeds of its like. He, glory be to Him, chose for this noble Prophet, because he is the most honoured of His creation, the purest of His servants in wives, children and companions. ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾ [Al ʿImran: 110]. "The best of you is my generation." And the nearer a person is to his heart (ﷺ), the purer he becomes. This proof is sufficient as evidence of the innocence of the Truthful One, may Allah be pleased with her.
