Since departing from their light after having become entangled with it, into darkness, is even more strange, He (exalted is He) followed what I have estimated, by means of what the context indicates most fully, with His saying, as a visible proof of that omitted matter, expressing wonder at those who were blind to the proofs of Divine Unity that He established, enumerated and clarified, to the extent that they became, as He (exalted is He) mentioned, greater than the light of the sun: ﴿They say﴾, that is, those to whom the light of God became manifest, with their tongues only: ﴿"We believe in God"﴾, who made His majesty, greatness and perfection clear to us, ﴿"and in the Messenger"﴾, whose perfect and universal message we have known through the proofs He established for it, ﴿"and we obey"﴾, that is, we bring about obedience to God and to the Messenger. He magnified the contradiction between deed and word by the particle of distance, saying: ﴿Then a party of them turns away﴾, that is, turns back by denial of the heart and turns away from obeying God and His Messenger, in error from the truth on their part, ﴿a party of them﴾ (p-296), that is, people who intend division from among those who uttered this statement.

Since the occurrence of apostasy from them, as has been indicated, should be in the utmost remoteness, even if it happens in the shortest time, He indicated it by the particle of delay, and affirmed that with His saying, affirming the preposition: ﴿after that﴾, that is, after this firm, strongly affirmed statement, along with God, who is greater than everything, and along with His Messenger, who is the most noble of creation. ﴿And those are not﴾, that is, the remote, hateful ones who, by their turning away, have come to be in a place of distance, ﴿believers﴾, that is, those perfect in faith in word and conviction. Rather, they are only of the people of the verbal attribute, stripped of the meaning of certainty.

When He had exposed them for what they concealed of their turning away, He then condemned what they displayed. So He said, expressing it with the particle of confirmation (ḥaqīq): ﴿And when they are called﴾, that is, those who claimed faith, by whatever caller it may be, ﴿to Allah﴾, that is, to what the Supreme King has established of His rulings, ﴿and His Messenger, that he may judge﴾, that is, the Messenger, ﴿between them﴾ by what Allah has shown him, ﴿behold, a party of them turn away﴾, that is, people naturally inclined to the harm that divides, ﴿turning away﴾, that is, they abruptly turned away, when the truth was against them, because of their following their desires, with a suddenness that indicates their firmness in it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 49:

﴿And if the right lies with them﴾ means: a firmly established state, ﴿with them﴾ meaning, by way of supposition, ﴿the truth﴾ meaning without any doubt, ﴿they come to him﴾ meaning to the Messenger, ﴿willingly submissive﴾ meaning yielding in the fullest submission, insofar as it agrees with their desires, because they know that he (ﷺ) turns with the truth, in their favour and against them, not out of obedience to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 50:

Since the cause of their act, after their display of obedience, was problematic, it was fitting to ask about it. So God, Exalted, said, clarifying it after alerting to the states it may involve: ﴿Is there in their hearts a disease?﴾ That is, a kind of corruption from the original nature (al-fitrah) that drives them to misguidance. ﴿Or have they come to doubt?﴾ That is, through a doubt that arose in them, blinding them to the path. ﴿Or﴾ there is no defect in them, neither original nor acquired, but the defect lies in the judge; so they ﴿fear that God should be unjust﴾ toward them, that is, that He should oppress, ﴿God﴾ who is independent of everything, because everything belongs to Him, ﴿against them﴾ by issuing an unjust ruling, and He is exempt from purposes; ﴿or His Messenger﴾ who does not speak from desire, by issuing a deviant command, and his infallibility from impurities is established.

Since none of that was the case, He turned away from it and said: ﴿Rather, those﴾ — that is, the distant, the hateful — ﴿they are﴾ — that is, exclusively — ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, that is, the perfect in wrongdoing, because their hearts are sealed upon disease and doubt, not that there is in them a single kind of it; and they do not fear injustice, rather it is their desire when the truth is against them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 51:

When He negated from them complete faith by the description He gave of them, it was as though He had been asked about the state of the believers, and so He said: ﴿The saying of the believers is only﴾, that is, always, ﴿the saying of the believers﴾, that is, the two groups in that attribute. The ten readers agreed on the accusative for "the saying" so that the noun of kāna would be the more definite of the two nouns, namely "an" (that) with what follows it, since it has no way to be made indefinite. It also resembles the pronoun, as Ibn Jinni said in al-Muhtasab, in that it cannot be described just as a pronoun cannot be described. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read it with the nominative according to one report, and so did Ibn Abi Ishaq according to one report. ﴿When they are called﴾, that is, by whatever caller, ﴿to Allah﴾, that is, to what the King, for whom there is no equal, has sent down of His rulings, ﴿and His Messenger, so that he may judge﴾, that is, Allah by what He has established of His rulings, or the Messenger ﷺ by what he addresses them with of his speech, ﴿between them﴾, that is, in some judgment of the judgments, whether in their favor or against them, ﴿that they say: "We hear"﴾, that is, the call, ﴿and we obey"﴾, that is, by answering Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

Since the implied sense was: "Then those are the believers," He joined to it His saying: ﴿And those﴾, that is, the people of high rank, ﴿they are﴾ exclusively ﴿the successful ones﴾, those whose description as believers was mentioned earlier at the beginning, as those who attain all that they hope for.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 52:

(p-٢٩٩) When He, glorified is He, linked success (falah) to this particular kind of obedience, He followed it with the general sense of obedience, saying: ﴿Whoever obeys Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all command belongs, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, that is, in submission to his decrees and others, in what displeases him and what pleases him, in all outward actions. ﴿And fears Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom majesty and honour belong, in his heart, for the sins he committed in the past, so that this fear drives him to every good. This was the practice of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all: when one of them fell into a shortcoming, he would come to the Prophet (ﷺ) saying, "Purify me," and one of them would be told to retract, but he would not retract. Purifying himself meant giving up his own self. This happened to their men and their women, may Allah be pleased with them all. May Allah grant us their way of life and gather us in their company. ﴿And keeps his duty to Him﴾, that is, keeps his duty to Allah regarding what lies ahead, by placing between himself and what angers Him a shield (wiqayah) against even permissible things, so that he abandons them out of scrupulousness (wara').

Since He used the singular pronouns, indicating how rare the obedient person is, He used the plural so that one would not think it refers to a single individual. He said: ﴿Those﴾, of elevated rank, ﴿are the ones who are successful﴾, with everlasting dominion, and there is no success for anyone other than them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 53:

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned what He had arranged as a consequence of outward obedience, which is the sign of inward submission, He mentioned the state of the hypocrites regarding it. He said, connecting it (ʿāṭifan) to ﴿they say﴾ [al-Nur: 47], because what is meant by it is nothing but the mere saying, without intending its restriction to a specific time: ﴿And they swear﴾. It seems that He expressed it in the past tense to indicate that they did not allow themselves to say it more than once, because of what this implies of increased humility and submission. ﴿By Allah﴾, that is, the King who possesses absolute perfection. He borrowed from the striving of the soul the phrase in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl): (p-300) ﴿with the utmost of their oaths﴾, that is, the utmost of swearing. ﴿If you command them﴾, that is, with some command among the affairs, ﴿they will surely go forth﴾ from what they are engaged in of its opposite, whatever it may be, to what you have commanded them. This was because they used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Wherever you are, we will be with you; if you go out, we go out; if you stay, we stay; and if you command us to fight, we will fight." Al-Baghawi reported this.

So it is as if it was said: What do you do in testing them? It was said: The matter is clearer than that, for every truth has a reality, and every act has its evidences. ﴿Say﴾, that is, to them: ﴿Do not swear﴾, that is, do not take oaths, for knowledge of what you are upon does not need swearing. But what moves you to go forth is love of compliance, not the obligation of an oath. In this there is an indication that they are deserving of accusation, and likewise al-Mutanabbi said:

*"In your oath concerning what you promise, there is what indicates that you are accused of breaking the promise."*

Then He gave the reason for that with His saying: ﴿Obedience is known﴾, that is, this reality is known ﴿from you and from others﴾. The intention of the reality is what permitted beginning with it while its wording is indefinite, because the generality it admits is, as they have said, among the most definite of definites. (p-301) It was not defined with "al" lest it be thought to refer to a prior mention or something similar. The meaning is that obedience, however much the servant strives to conceal it, its signs must appear upon his features; and likewise disobedience, because "No servant conceals an inner secret except that Allah clothes him in its garment," narrated by al-Tabarani from Jundub, may Allah be pleased with him. Musaddad narrated from Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "If a man enters a room inside a room and persists there in an act, people will soon speak of it. No doer does any deed except that Allah clothes him in the garment of his deed: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil."

And Abu Ya'la and al-Hakim, who said: "Its chain is sound, though they did not record it," narrated from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "If one of you were to work upon a solid rock with no door or window, his deed would come out to the people, whatever it may be." Then he gave the reason for his manifesting of what is hidden with his saying: ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, that is, the One who has encompassing knowledge of everything, ﴿is Acquainted with what you do﴾, even if you strive to conceal it, for He sets up signs upon it by which He makes it known to His servants. So the oath does not avail the one who swears, and submission does not harm the Muslim.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 54:

When he had alerted to their deception, he indicated that their profession of faith should not be relied upon, and that the testimony of their outward marks (al-tawassum) concerning them was to be accepted. He commanded that they be encouraged and warned, pointing to turning away from their punishment, so he said: ﴿Say: Obey Allah﴾, O you who have professed faith, ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses absolute perfection, ﴿and obey the Messenger﴾, that is, the one who holds the absolute mission, outwardly and inwardly, unlike the hypocrites. ﴿But if you turn away﴾, that is, if turning away occurs from you in disobedience to him, even in the slightest form of turning away, as indicated by the deletion of the taa' (in the verb), ﴿you will be misguided, and you will harm only yourselves﴾. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Then upon him is only that with which he has been charged﴾, that is, the Messenger, with the conveying (al-tabligh) of which he has been charged by One who, when He charges anyone with something, must have that thing carried out for Him or something heavier than it; ﴿and upon you is that with which you have been charged﴾, namely acceptance, and it is not incumbent upon him to compel you to guidance. By His saying: ﴿And if you obey him﴾, that is, by turning wholeheartedly to everything he commands you, ﴿you will be guided﴾, that is, to every good, He implies that there is no guidance for them without following him.

Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad narrated in the Zawa'id of the Musnad, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said from the pulpit: "Whoever does not give thanks for the little does not give thanks for the much; whoever does not give thanks to people does not give thanks to Allah. Speaking of the blessing of Allah is thankfulness, and neglecting it is disbelief. Community (al-jama'ah) is mercy, and division is punishment." He said: Abu Umamah al-Bahili (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Hold to the great majority (al-sawad al-a'zam)!" He said: A man said: "What is the great majority?" Then Abu Umamah recited this verse in Surah al-Nur: ﴿But if they turn away, then upon him is only that with which he has been charged, and upon you is that with which you have been charged﴾.

Since what the Messenger (ﷺ) was charged with was unspecified, He specified it by His saying: ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾, that is, from any other source, ﴿the clear conveyance﴾, that is, the conveying by which delivery is achieved without doubt, whether by clarification alone or combined with the sword and what is below it of kinds of deterrents.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 55:

When this permission became evident, namely the restraint from killing the hypocrites (al-munafiqun) for the Prophet (ﷺ), lest people say, "Muhammad sought help from a people, and when God gave him victory through them, he began to kill them," and so whoever hears that would refrain from entering Islam, then the harm of killing them would be greater than the harm of leaving them alone. This is because the religion was not yet so firmly established that such a thing would have no effect on it. Souls then longed to know whether this state would continue. So God removed this distress from both of them through His saying, as an explanation that the establishment of the religion does not depend on them, whether they turn toward it or turn away: ﴿God has promised﴾, that is, He who has encompassing knowledge of everything, ﴿to those of you who believe﴾. This, along with that, is like a reason for what came before it, an encouragement for whoever looks at the worldly life with some degree of reflection. He restricted it with His saying ﴿of you﴾, explicitly referring to the people of the first generation, so that it would be clear in excluding the hypocrites who turn away in aversion, as an indication that they will continue in humiliation and lowliness. He placed this restriction first, giving it attention because of what has been mentioned, unlike what comes in Surah al-Fath. ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾, confirming their faith, ﴿the righteous deeds﴾, such as submission to the rulings and other things. He emphasized this with the utmost emphasis through the oath particle, because most people have doubt about that, so He said: ﴿He will surely grant them succession in the earth﴾, that is, the land of the Arabs and the non-Arabs, by extending their time and implementing their rulings. ﴿Just as He granted succession﴾, that is, He sought and brought about a succession through their existence, ﴿to those before them﴾, that is, among the nations, among the Children of Israel and others, from every people who was given authority and prevailed over enemies after severe weakness, as He wrote in the Psalms (al-Zabur): ﴿that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya': 105], and as Moses, peace be upon him, said: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to God; He causes whomever He wills of His servants to inherit it, and the final outcome is for the righteous﴾ [al-A'raf: 128]. ﴿And He will surely establish for them﴾, that is, both inwardly and outwardly, ﴿their religion﴾. He attributed it to them as an indication of the firmness of their footing in it, and that it is perpetual and not abrogated (yunsakh). ﴿Which He has approved for them﴾, so that they may establish the prescribed punishments (hudud) within it, such as execution and others, upon the noble and the lowly alike, whether those who commit them are a group or not. They show favoritism to no one and fear no blame of a blamer, because at that time the turning away of one who turns away will not harm it, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning the Harurites (al-Haruriyya) in their entirety: "Indeed, if I reach them, I will surely kill them with the killing of 'Ad," after he refrained from killing their leader, and forbade killing him, and he was one man at the Battle of Hunayn.

When He gave them the good news of establishment, He indicated its extent to them through His saying: ﴿And He will surely change them﴾, and He indicated that this general security does not encompass all time by affirming the preposition, so He said: ﴿after their fear﴾, this in which they are now, ﴿into security﴾, that is, a great security proportionate to this fear, during the time of prophethood and its succession. Then He followed that with its result, by His saying as a reason for the establishment and what accompanies it: ﴿They worship Me﴾, that is, Me alone. He stated the intended meaning clearly, explaining the state of beneficial worship, by His saying: ﴿They do not associate anything with Me﴾, outwardly or inwardly, because their time will be a time of justice, so they will not love one another in it through desire or fear. Al-Tabarani narrated in al-Awsat from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may God be pleased with him, who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, may God be pleased with them, came to Medina, and the Ansar, may God be pleased with them all, sheltered them, the Arabs shot at them from one bow, and then this verse was revealed: ﴿He will surely grant them succession in the earth﴾," and so on to the end of the verse. God, glorified is He, has indeed spoken truly, and who is more truthful in statement than God? He opened the lands for them and gave them victory over the tyrants of the servants. They humbled the necks of the Chosroes (al-Akasira) and enslaved the sons of the Caesars (al-Qayasira), and they were empowered from east to west with an empowerment that had not been given before them to any nation among the nations, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God folded the earth for me, so I saw its easts and its wests, and the dominion of my nation will reach what was folded for me of it." Whoever studies the conquests of the lands knows this. The most comprehensive and best of them is the second half of the biography of the memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu al-Rabi' ibn Salim al-Kila'i, and the book of his teacher Ibn Hubaysh is also comprehensive. I know of nothing more beneficial for the firmness of faith, after memorizing the Qur'an, than studying the biographies (siyar) and conquests, and the biography of al-Kila'i combines both aspects. My versified composition of the biography is in the qasida whose beginning is:

"What is the matter with your eyelid, overflowing with tears, and the sea of your thought, abundant in concern, is full?"

It is the most comprehensive of the biographies. May God make the completion of its explanation easy, Amin.

When they killed Uthman, may God be pleased with him, and rebelled against Ali, then his son al-Hasan, may God be pleased with them both, God removed that security, as was indicated by "min" (from) and the indefiniteness of "amnan" (security). Fear came and continued, extending and increasing little by little, until in our time it has become a great matter. And God is the One sought for help.

Since the presumed meaning is: whoever remains steadfast upon the religion of Islam, submits to its rulings, and remains upright, attains this good news, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾, that is, by turning away from the rulings or other things. Or it is a conjunction with ﴿they worship Me﴾, because its meaning is: and whoever does not worship Me.

Since the complete wrongdoer (al-fasiq al-kamil) is only one who dies upon his disbelief, so his deeds are nullified, his disbelief thereby encompasses his entire time, unlike one who dies a Muslim, even if he was a disbeliever in everything that passed for him before that. He dropped the preposition and said: ﴿after that﴾, that is, after this great succession in the manner explained, ﴿those﴾, the ones far removed from good, ﴿they are﴾ exclusively ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those who have gone out of the religion with complete departure, with whom no excuse is accepted, and no slip is overlooked for its companion. Rather, the rulings are enforced upon them, by execution and other things, and no blame is considered regarding them, and no compassion takes them at the time of retribution, as was mentioned at the beginning of the surah concerning one who is liable to be flogged. Perhaps the verse is indicating the people of apostasy (ahl al-ridda).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 56:

When this good news was complete, and the implied sense was: "So act and worship," he conjoined to it His saying: ﴿And establish the prayer﴾, meaning, for it is the pillar (qiwam) of what is between you and your Lord. Yet its conjunction could also be to His saying ﴿Obey Allah﴾ [al-Nur: 54], in which case it falls under the speech of "Say" (qul). ﴿And give zakat﴾, for it is the order (nizam) of what is between you and your brothers. ﴿And obey the Messenger﴾, meaning the one who encompasses the Message in everything he commands you with, for what he commands is only by the command of your Lord. ﴿That you may be shown mercy﴾, meaning, so that you may be among those who, ignorant of the outcomes, hope to attain mercy from One who, in reality, has no merciful one other than Him. (p-308)

Since the disbelievers were so numerous and powerful, the situation called for emphasizing the meaning of establishment (al-tamkin) of the believers' rule, as an answer to a question as if one had said: "Is that possible?" So He said: ﴿Do not think﴾, that is, O listener, ﴿that those who disbelieved﴾, that is, even if their numbers increase beyond counting and their greatness exceeds all bounds, for that assumption is a sign of weakness of intellect, because a king is not incapacitated by those under his domination. It is also permissible that this be an address to the Prophet (ﷺ) for the sake of further affirming it, because the fulfilment of the promise is in proportion to the greatness of the one addressed. ﴿Incapable﴾ of [overcoming] Our friends ﴿in the earth﴾, for they are certainly seized. ﴿And their refuge﴾, that is, their dwelling and abode after the seizing, ﴿is the Fire﴾. Since the dwelling in a thing cannot occur except after arriving at it, He said: ﴿And how evil is the destination!﴾ — the destination of it! So how much more so when it is by way of dwelling.

When [human] weariness is one of the dispositions of the souls, the gradual introduction of speech on its aims, especially rulings, bit by bit amid other aims, falls more deeply into the heart and is more appealing to the nature. This is especially so when it comes in forms of wondrous correspondences and kinds of connections that are, despite their subtlety, strange. Allah adorned the rooting of these [rulings] by their detailing. He began the surah with a group of them, and separated them with the pearls of admonition, the gems of wisdom, (p-309) and the urging towards lofty morals and noble deeds. Then He connected it with the divine matters, which are its roots, and from whose exalted stations its chapters branch out. When He concluded it with the establishment of the people of this religion and the weakening of the affair of the transgressors, He proceeded to complete it by establishing the rest of its conditions, as confirmation of what He had decreed of establishment, and of what He had concluded of weakening, and as a warning against what He had concluded of the humiliating punishment, and as a verification of what was obligated upon them of obedience and adherence to the Sunnah and the community. So He said, connecting with what He had concluded the earlier rulings with, of the command to marry off the unmarried, and the restraint from compelling the prostitutes, following those who had not yet come to know the private parts of women: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, i.e., from among the men and the women, either by way of prevailing the masculine, or because women are more fitted to guard the ʿawra (private parts, nakedness). ﴿Let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission﴾, in confirmation of the claim of faith, [meaning] the slaves and the female slaves who have reached maturity, and those close to them, to enter upon you, out of dislike of looking upon your private parts and of the approach through that to your displeasure. ﴿And those﴾ who have come to know the private parts of women, but ﴿have not reached puberty﴾ [of] ﴿you﴾ — he restricted it with His saying ﴿among you﴾ to exclude the enslaved and the disbelievers — ﴿three times﴾ in each period. It is also possible that what is meant is three requests for permission each time. If permission is not granted, the one seeking permission returns as was previously stated. The first time is (p-310) of the three periods: ﴿before the prayer of dawn﴾, because it is the time of rising from the beds and removing the garments of sleep. The second is ﴿and when you put off your clothes﴾, i.e., those meant for going out among people, ﴿at midday﴾, for the midday rest. The third is ﴿and after the prayer of ʿishā'﴾, because it is the time of separation from the garments of wakefulness and the joining with the garments of sleep. He singled out these times because they are the hours of privacy and the removal of garments. He mentioned "min" in the two places to indicate the nearness of the time to the mentioned time, to fix it, and He omitted it in the middle one to indicate its extent, because it is not fixed. Then He gave the reason for that with His saying: ﴿three times of nakedness﴾, i.e., lapses in concealment and guarding. The root of ʿawra (nakedness), as al-Bayḍāwī said, is "defect" or "flaw".

It is called so because in them the nakedness shows. ﴿For you﴾, because they are the hours of removing garments and of privacy with the family. He stated the ruling for other than that with His saying, in a resumptive manner: ﴿There is no blame on you﴾, i.e., in leaving off the command, ﴿nor on them﴾, meaning the slaves, the servants, and the children, in leaving off the seeking of permission, ﴿any blame﴾, i.e., sin — its root is inclination — ﴿beyond these﴾, i.e., at all times other than these, when they come in upon you. Then he gave the reason for the permissibility at other times, (p-311) excluding others, clarifying that the wisdom of seeking permission at every time, as has passed, is with His saying: ﴿They are frequent attendants upon you﴾, i.e., for a task of service that you need, just as you are frequent attendants upon them for the task that sets right their affairs and yours in employing them. ﴿Some of you﴾ are frequent attendants ﴿upon others﴾, for the task that the other is unable to do or finds burdensome. So if the command of seeking permission were general, it would lead to hardship.

When Allah, glorified is He, raised the clarification in these verses to a degree that exceeds human capacity — especially since they concern rulings, and speech on them wearies the people of eloquence — and since the hearer, given what he has been created with of forgetfulness, becomes oblivious that this is the manner of the whole Qur'an, He said, pointing to the greatness of its matter in its distinction and its clarification: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., like this clarification, ﴿Allah makes clear﴾, with what He has of all-encompassing knowledge and power, ﴿to you﴾, O community of the specially chosen, ﴿the signs﴾ in the rulings and other things, by His knowledge and His wisdom. ﴿And Allah﴾, to whom belongs the all-encompassing comprehension of everything, ﴿is All-Knowing﴾ of everything, ﴿All-Wise﴾, who perfects what He wills, so no one can annul it. Concluding the verse with this attribute indicates that it is muhkam (firmly established), not abrogated, as al-Sha'bi and others said. This was conveyed by Ibn Kathir, and something similar is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

(p-312) When He had explained the ruling concerning the children and the slaves, who are the most obedient to the command and the most receptive to every good, He followed it with the ruling concerning the adult free persons, saying: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty﴾, i.e., among your free ones, ﴿the age of puberty (ḥulum)﴾, i.e., the age at which emission of semen occurs through seeing intercourse in sleep. This is its basic meaning, but what is intended is the age of emission in general. ﴿let them ask permission﴾ before entering upon others, at all times, ﴿as those before them asked permission﴾, as He explained at the beginning of the verses saying: ﴿Do not enter houses other than your own until you have sought permission and greeted their occupants﴾ [al-Nur: 27]. Ibn Kathir transmitted from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that when the boy has reached the age of four, he asks permission during the three times of privacy (al-'awrat ath-thalath) before his parents; but when he reaches puberty, he must ask permission in every circumstance.

Since the verses on seeking permission are the most perfect means of cutting off the sources of evil, and abandoning them is the greatest opener of the doors of trials, and since bringing forth speech on the rulings of the lawful and the unlawful, together with refinement and clarification, is in the extreme of difficulty, and weaning souls from what they have become accustomed to is extremely arduous, He, glory be to Him, alluded to this by repeating the verse of clarification, indicating that it—because of its exalted status—deserves emphasis, and that eloquent speakers regard the capacity for clarification as remote whenever it is desired in this manner.

(p-313) So He said: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., like that clarification which He made in the verses of rulings, ﴿Allah makes clear﴾, with His attributes of perfection, ﴿to you﴾, together with your deficiencies, ﴿His signs﴾, i.e., the indications pointing to Him, from these subsidiary matters and what the fundamental matters ascend to. He attributed them to Himself, glory be to Him, in exaltation of them, indicating that they are a prelude to the divine matters, for whoever is not free of the troubles of thoughts will not fly to that airfield. It also urges reflection upon what preceded of them, to recall the ruling to which they called and the admonitions they distinguished, and it draws attention to the beneficial sciences they contain, both for religion and for the world. It further increases the encouragement toward knowledge and wisdom, indicating that this is the cause of every happiness. So He said: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, i.e., encompassing everything. al-Tabarani and others narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When it was morning, I had a wet dream, so I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ and informed him that I had had a wet dream. He said: 'Do not enter upon the women.' Never did a day come upon me that was more difficult than that one."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 24, verse 60:

When He, glorified be He, mentioned the flourishing of youth in the context of changing the ruling on the hijab, He followed it with the ruling concerning the time of youth's decline, regarding the laying aside of outer garments. So He said: ﴿And women past child-bearing﴾, and He confirmed the matter with His words: ﴿of women﴾. Al-qawa'id (ﷺ) is the plural of qa'id, and they are the women who have ceased from bearing children, from menstruation, and from marriage, due to old age. Since this last matter is its pivot, He said: ﴿who have no hope of marriage﴾, i.e., because they have no desire for it, or because they have reached an age at which they are no longer desired. ﴿Then there is no blame upon them﴾, i.e., no sin of hardship, ﴿in laying aside their outer garments﴾, i.e., the outer garments worn over the concealing clothes in the presence of men. The evidence for this is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him: "from their garments." Abu Salih said: she puts down the jilbab, which is what covers her clothing from above, like a mantle, and she stands before a man in her shift and head-covering. ﴿Without displaying adornment﴾, i.e., deliberately—by laying aside what has been permitted to them—displaying their faces together with adornment; or, not making a show of adornment. In the combination of al-'Subab and al-Muhkam it says: "The woman tabarrajat: she displayed her face." And in al-Qamus: "Tabarrajat: she displayed her adornment to men," end of quote.

The root b-r-j revolves around the notion of appearing, as has passed in al-Hijr. Al-Baydawi said: The basic meaning of al-barj is affectation in displaying what is hidden, end of quote. It seems that the form of tafa''ul (tabarruj) was used to indicate that what appears of her face or adornment unintentionally, not aimed at corruption, is not a sin.

When He mentioned what is permissible, and the displaying of the face is a means to suspicion, He pointed to it, mentioning what is recommended, to urge the choice of the best and finest deeds: ﴿And that they refrain [from it] is better for them﴾, i.e., that they seek chastity by continuing to cover and not lightening their dress by casting off the outer cloak and head-covering, ﴿is better for them﴾ than the casting off mentioned.

Since the situation of these women regarding mingling in that described manner is known to not be free of speech, the implied meaning is: Allah, in lifting hardship from them, is Compassionate and Merciful toward them. He followed this with His words: ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., He to whom belong all attributes of perfection, ﴿is Hearing﴾, i.e., of their speech when they address men: whether they are submissive in it and affect softening of the voice, or whether they speak in the known, unobjectionable manner; ﴿Knowing﴾ of what they intend by it and of everything.

[p-316] When Allah, glorified is He, had completed what He mentioned concerning the sanctity of homes, which entails the protection of chastity in a way that necessarily secures property, He followed it with what is permitted of that for eating, which is among the most important purposes of property, whether eaten together or alone. He said, in answer to one who seems to have asked: Is this restriction on homes applicable to relatives and others in all circumstances?

﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾, that is, in eating with others and in what follows of the rulings, even if others dislike his eating because he reaches out his hand however it happens to fall, for he is pitied. Seeking permission is for the sake of sight. ﴿Nor upon the lame﴾, whose condition is not expected to improve, ﴿is there any blame﴾, even if some of the affluent find him repugnant, for he shares with the others the fact that he is to be shown mercy because of his deficiency. ﴿Nor upon the sick﴾, that is, one whose illness is expected to be cured, whether it is with lameness or otherwise, ﴿is there any blame﴾, likewise because of his illness. He mentioned him last because of the hope of his recovery. ﴿Nor upon yourselves﴾, that is, nor upon anyone other than those mentioned. He expressed it this way as a reminder that all are from one self. ﴿That you eat from your houses﴾, that is, the houses in which your dependents are. He mentioned them, glorified is He, so that no suspicion would arise from leaving them if one left them. The houses of your children are also included in this, because they are from the earnings of the father: "The best of what a man eats is from his earnings, and his child is from his earnings," and "You and your property belong to your father." ﴿Or the houses of your fathers﴾, however distant your lineages are; perhaps He used the plural for this reason, for they are your upbringers and their sanctity is your sanctity. ﴿Or the houses of your mothers﴾, likewise. He placed the father first because he is the most honoured, and he is always the master of his house, and the property is his. ﴿Or the houses of your brothers﴾, whether full, paternal or maternal brothers, by lineage or by fosterage, for they are the most worthy of those who are content with this after the parents, since they are your full siblings, and they are the guardians of their own houses. ﴿Or the houses of your sisters﴾, for they come after them, because the guardian of the house, if they are married, is the husband. ﴿Or the houses of your paternal uncles﴾, for they are the full siblings of your fathers, whether they are full siblings, paternal or maternal. Had he mentioned only the paternal uncle, it might have been assumed that he meant only the full sibling, but he is most entitled to the name. ﴿Or the houses of your paternal aunts﴾, who come after the uncles because of their weakness, and because their guardians are perhaps their husbands. ﴿Or the houses of your maternal uncles﴾, because they are the full siblings of your mothers. ﴿Or the houses of your maternal aunts﴾; He placed them last for the reason mentioned. ﴿Or what you hold the keys to﴾, that is, the disposal of it in any manner, such as by agency. ﴿Or your friend﴾ whose consent to this you know, even by a sign, as is generally the case. For this reason He stated it without restriction, even if you did not have his key but his dependents were in it. All of this is without corruption, without carrying away, and without hoarding. Here He placed the friend on a par with the relative, to draw attention to the noble rank of friendship, its subtle secret, and its lightness of affair, and He mentioned him singly because of his rarity. It is related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad: "Among the greatness of the sanctity of a friend is that He made him like the self, the father, and those with him." Al-Isfahani said: "They have said: When the outward condition indicates the owner's consent, that stands in place of explicit permission, and what makes seeking permission ugly and burdensome is like one who has been served food and asks his companion's permission to eat."

When He mentioned the place of eating, He mentioned the state of the one eating, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾, that is, no sin, which by its nature would turn its doer away from equity, ﴿that you eat together﴾, that is, in company, even if among you there is one with a defect in his make, because whoever is exposed to misfortunes is worthy of having mercy on the afflicted, so he should not find him repugnant, out of fear of the reversal of circumstances. [p-318] When He encouraged, at the beginning of Islam, when most people were in hardship, toward consolation and gathering with guests, as an encouragement which was thought to be obligatory, together with their generosity which prompts generosity and gathering for the comfort of the needy, He lightened it for them by His saying: ﴿or in groups﴾, that is, dispersed, without intent of disdain, arrogance, or harm. Although eating in company is better and more blessed, as its being mentioned first implies, Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah related from Wahshi ibn Harb, from his father, from his grandfather, that a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We eat but are not satisfied." He said: "Perhaps you eat separately? Gather around your food and mention the name of Allah, and He will bless it for you." Ibn Majah related from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Eat together and do not separate, for blessing is with the group."

When He mentioned the place of eating and its manner, He mentioned the condition in which the one entering those places, or others, is to be, saying, as a consequence of the permission already mentioned, with the particle of confirmation, as glad tidings that they would obey after they had been reluctant about this when Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Do not devour your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾ [al-Nisa: 29]. ﴿So when you enter houses﴾, that is, because of that or otherwise, ﴿houses﴾, that is, houses in which entry is permitted, whatever houses they are, owned or not, mosques or others, ﴿then greet﴾ immediately upon entering ﴿one another﴾ [p-319], that is, its people, who are of your religion and nearness. He expressed it this way to encourage greeting and good treatment in honouring. And so that the expression would fit the case where no one is inside, in which case one says: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah," and this falls within both literal and figurative usage. ﴿As a greeting﴾, a verbal noun from the meaning rather than the wording, or they invoke for the one greeting safety, life, and the possession of lasting existence. ﴿From Allah﴾, that is, it is worthy, for the completeness of its goodness, to be attributed to Him to whom all perfection belongs, glorified is He. ﴿Blessed﴾, that is, established with the greatest firmness, by being in accordance with what Allah has legislated, from the sincere hearts of you. ﴿Good﴾, delighting the hearing. Then He described the clarity, drawing attention to the beauty and excellence in these verses, and He said, beginning anew as has passed more than once: ﴿Thus﴾, that is, like this clarification, great in its importance, ﴿Allah makes clear﴾, that is, He who encompasses everything, ﴿the signs for you﴾, than which there is no more perfect.

Since Allah, exalted is He, by His knowledge, wisdom, might, power, subtle kindness and expertise, created a luminous intellect which guides to the truth and to a straight path, and distributed it among His servants, and created in them kinds of obstacles to that intellect preventing it from proceeding upon the course of uprightness, namely desire, laziness, slackness and boredom, He made them veils which screen it from proceeding, conceal from it the faculties, and prevent it from reaching, except through disciplines and struggles in which powers grow weary and resolves weaken. So the skilled among them hardly constructs a sound syllogism, because of his error in the premises, and the conclusion then is corrupt in foundation and weak in base. Thus they never ceased to differ, until difference led them to enmities, quarrels and strife, which drew them to the sword, the loss of souls and the perishing of lives. So Allah, glorified is He, sent down for them at every time a law suited to that era, upon the tongue of one of His messengers, peace and blessings be upon them. That law was made to accord with sound reason, bright light, a flowing spring and a strong cause. Whoever holds fast to it is guided and does not go astray. In it He set down limits and established deterrents, so that His wisdom would appear and His knowledge and power become manifest. Thus they became laws agreeing in their principles and differing in their branches according to the times, as an indication that the agent in changing rulings according to the times is one, who chooses, and as a trial for the servants, to distinguish the righteous among them from the corrupt. Raiding upon any of the honours or properties without what He permitted [p-321] causes intellects to depart and insights to blind. He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿So that you may understand﴾, that is, that you may be in hope, in the presence of the One whose hope is valid, of the persistence of this attribute in you, which is the restraint of souls and their turning back from desires, by following the signs of the law which He sent down, He who repeated His description here as All-Knowing, All-Wise. So do not turn away after your saying ﴿We hear and we obey﴾ [al-Nur: 51], from submitting to the rulings while you are averse.

(p-322) Since He, glory be to Him, had negated faith from them through turning away from the rulings, and followed it with what you see Him arrange in the best order, until He concluded with what hints that whoever is blind to His rulings after this clarification has had his intellect taken away, and He repeated the mention of clarification (*bayan*) in this surah, a repetition that pointed to the radiance of the meanings with the firmest of fingers, until they became embodied for the eye to see, and He explained who attains the description of faith through the good manner of seeking permission, and the command of the Messenger (ﷺ) was the most exalted abode, one in which residence is obligatory and every other homeland is abandoned, so that the earth, despite its vastness, becomes narrow for its sake, and its traversal is forbidden because of him, in the position of another's house which may not be entered without permission, He said, defining this by way of restriction (*hasr*, exclusivity), in contrast to the negation of ﴿And those are not believers﴾ [al-Nur: 47], clarifying the great offense of leaving the assembly of the Prophet (ﷺ), which calls for gathering, without permission:

﴿Indeed, the believers﴾, that is, the perfect ones, who will have success (p-322) ﴿are those who have believed in Allah﴾, that is, the King, the Most High, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, outwardly and inwardly.

Since the discourse was about those firmly grounded (*al-rasikhun*), the place called for the particle of confirmation (*adat al-tahqiq*), so He said: ﴿And when﴾, that is, and when they truly affirm their faith by being such that, when they ﴿are with him﴾, that is, the Messenger (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), ﴿on a matter of common concern﴾, that is, a matter upon which they gather before Allah, such as jihad against the enemies of Allah, consultation about an important affair, the Friday prayer, and the like, ﴿they do not depart﴾ from that matter by a single step to any place on earth, even to their own homes, for anything whatsoever, even if it were among their most important affairs, because He has taken from them a covenant of obedience in hardship and ease, in what they like and what they dislike, ﴿until they seek his permission﴾, so that he grants them leave, because the one commanded has become their abode, their refuge and their place of settling, and everything else, of places and affairs, has become his, peace be upon him, not theirs, having no share for them in it, so it is not lawful for them to enter it, physically or in meaning, except with his permission. This is from the great alerting to the loftiness of his command and the nobility of his rank. For He, glory be to Him, just as He commanded them to seek permission when entering upon him and upon others, singled out seeking his permission for departing from him (ﷺ), and made the rank of this immediately following the rank of faith in Allah and His Messenger, and made them like its cause, with the sentence opening with the particle of restriction, and placing the believers in a subject (*mubtada'*) whose predicate is a relative clause whose connection encompasses the three ranks, explaining it.

(p-323) When He negated from the believers going away until they seek permission, He conveyed that one who seeks permission is a believer, and He stated this implication explicitly so that it would be more emphatic, saying, emphasizing the gravity of neglecting courtesy before him (ﷺ), and confirming the preservation of his sanctity and courtesy with him, lest his thought be disturbed by another manner, and clarifying that seeking permission is the true proof of faith:

﴿Indeed, those who seek your permission﴾, that is, ask your leave for themselves when they wish to depart, in some of their affairs which may be expected to keep them from it, ﴿those are﴾ especially the high-ranking ones ﴿who believe﴾, that is, who bring faith into existence at all times ﴿in Allah﴾, to whom belongs the whole command, so there is no equal to Him, ﴿and His Messenger﴾. And this gathers the scattered qualities of faith.

When He restricted them to seeking permission, there followed from this His informing him (ﷺ) of what he does at that time, so He said:

﴿So when they seek your permission﴾, that is, these whose claim is true; and He emphasized it upon them, to magnify courtesy with him (ﷺ), by His saying ﴿for some of their affairs﴾, which is what the need for it is most pressing, ﴿then permit whom you will among them﴾. It was said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended the pulpit on Friday, whoever wished to leave for an excuse would stand in front of him, and he would know that he was seeking permission, and he would grant leave to whomever he wished." Mujahid said: The permission of the imam on Friday is that he gestures with his hand. And it was said: Likewise it should be with the people and their imams and leaders (p-324) in religion and knowledge, that they not forsake them in any calamity among calamities.

When He established for him, by this entrusting, a nobility that his description cannot reach, He made them understand that the state of one who seeks permission is deficient compared to the state of one who entrusts himself and remains constantly, whatever their condition, so He said:

﴿And ask forgiveness for them from Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses absolute self-sufficiency, so no obedience benefits Him, and no disobedience harms Him. Or the statement may be inclusive of one whose claim is true and others. Then He gave the reason for that, encouraging seeking forgiveness and comforting the hearts of the people of sins, by His saying:

﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One possessing the attributes of perfection, ﴿is Forgiving﴾, that is, He has this attribute, so He is worthy of forgiving them what they fell short in, ﴿Merciful﴾, that is, everything He commands them is good for them, even if its opposite appears to them.

When this surah, in its generality, and these verses, in their particularity, had made manifest the nobility of the Messenger that dazzled minds, on account of what the hypocrite had done in daring to act against that lofty dignity and that most perfect rank, and since it was known from this that he ﷺ has in all his affairs and every aspect of his state a distinction that belongs to no one else, Allah stated this explicitly, to magnify the matter and exalt his station, so that whoever defended the hypocrite, or was slack in his affair and fell short of the reach of the foremost (ahl al-sawabiq), might learn good manners. He said, alerting that calamities are a cause for the manifestation of virtues or the exposure of faults: ﴿Do not make﴾, that is, O you who believe, ﴿the summoning of the Messenger﴾, that is, the summons he issues to you, ﴿among you﴾ (p-325) even if in the general sense, regarding the obligation to comply, ﴿like the summoning of some of you by others﴾. For his command is great, and opposing it out of disdain is disbelief. Nor should you make your summoning of him like the summoning of one of you by another, merely by name; rather, show him good manners through glorifying, honoring and magnifying him, as Allah has prescribed, with such phrases as: O Prophet, O Messenger, along with displaying courtesy in the manner of speech and action, by lowering the voice and humility.

Since some of them would show agreement while concealing opposition, He warned against this by the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and the completeness of His power. He said, giving the reason, emphasizing, confirming, and informing, by renewing the attachment of knowledge of witnessing (al-ʿilm al-shuhudi, knowledge that is present and observed) whenever anyone renews a betrayal, for the continuing attribute of His encompassing knowledge, without regard to time: ﴿Allah certainly knows﴾, that is, He who possesses all the attributes of glory, if you assume that what you do by concealment hides your affair from His Messenger ﷺ, then He, glorified is He, knows ﴿those of you who slip away﴾. He specified those deserving rebuke by His saying ﴿of you﴾, that is, who strain to slip away from themselves so as to make their departure as hidden as possible, ﴿furtively﴾, that is, slipping away while hiding from him, with some of them concealing themselves behind others. It is said: laadha bi-l-shay'i lawdhan, liwadhan, and mulawadhah: he took cover and sheltered himself. So it is a verbal noun (masdar) of tasallala, though not from its own root. Perhaps He introduced ﴿qad﴾ before the present tense to increase the certainty of those who verify, and to open a path of possibility for those with doubt, for the fear of punishment is sufficiently provoked by the mere occurrence of possibility.

He made the consequence of His knowledge His saying: (p-326) ﴿Let those beware﴾, that is, let them be cautious, ﴿who oppose﴾, that is, who carry out opposition by going away, passing beyond and turning aside, ﴿his command﴾, that is, the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, toward its contrary, ﴿lest a trial befall them﴾, that is, something that mixes into them in this world, so that it turns their affairs away from the beloved state in which they had been, ﴿or a painful punishment afflict them﴾ in the Hereafter. This indicates that the command is for obligation unless a diverting indicator turns it away, because the threat of punishment for neglecting it establishes that. For warning against punishment only occurs after the cause for the descent of punishment has been established.

When He, glorified is He, had established the proofs that He is the Light of the heavens and the earth, since nothing subsists except through Him, glorified is He, and had concluded with a warning to every opponent, this produced the consequence that everything belongs to Him. So He said: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs﴾, that is, the One to whom all glory belongs, all of ﴿what is in the heavens﴾, and ﴿the earth﴾. Because it is established that He, glorified is He, encompasses all knowledge and power, the context did not call for emphasis by repeating the relative pronoun. That is, ﴿the earth﴾ means both substance (jawhar) and accident ('arad), and both belong to Him as well, because the earth is within the heaven, and each heaven is within the one above it, until this reaches the Throne, which He has stated in more than one verse is His, and which is also a heaven because of its elevation above what is below it. Therefore, everything in it belongs to Him. This is more eloquent, because it indicates ownership through metaphor (majaz), than if it had been stated explicitly. Thus this indicates, after the indication of His existence, His oneness, and the perfection of His knowledge and power.

Since their conditions are among the things that belong to Him, it is known that they did not subsist in their origin, nor do they have any continuance, except by His knowledge, and because they are by His creation. Therefore He said, affirming, emphasizing, and instilling awe: ﴿Indeed He knows what you are﴾, O people, all of you, ﴿upon﴾, that is, now. The intended meaning of the present tense here is the existence of the attribute without regard to time; had He expressed it in the past tense, it would have been thought to be restricted to the past. The discussion about the particle "qad" (indeed) being placed before it is as has passed just now, with regard to those who are powerful in sight and those who are weak and turbid. ﴿And the Day﴾, that is, and He knows what they are upon on the Day when ﴿they are returned﴾, that is, by the compulsion of an overpowering Compeller over them in that state, they being unable to resist Him or to exercise any kind of refusal, ﴿to Him﴾. The original wording would have been "what you are upon", but He turned away from them to magnify the matter. Or this may be specific to those who turn away and oppose, indicating that they will be subjected to a strict reckoning. The secret of the shift in address (iltifat) is to draw attention to turning away from the one who denies the Resurrection and to turning toward the one who affirms it, in order to protect the precious words from the rude, the foolish, and the base. ﴿Then He will inform them﴾, that is, as a consequence of that He will inform them with a great informing ﴿of what they did﴾, so let them prepare an answer for every part of it. ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One who has complete comprehension ﴿of everything﴾ of that and other things ﴿is All-Knowing﴾. Therefore He sent down the clear signs, and He is the light of the earth and the heavens. Thus He has joined the conclusion to the beginning, and the end has been fastened to the start. And Allah is the Guide.
